1689327113.whyB: 4 halves the time because there are half as many chefs, but there are also half as many dishes.
1689327113.whyC: 16 doubles the time for fewer chefs but forgets there are fewer dishes too.
1689327113.whyD: 12 has no basis; each chef cooks 1 dish in 8 minutes, so 4 chefs cook 4 dishes in 8 minutes.
1689327113.explanationTl: Isang chef = 1 dish sa 8 minutes. Kaya 4 chefs = 4 dishes sa 8 minutes din.

14256358.hint: Which kind of speech would make people listen closely and not want it to end?
14256358.whyA: Monotonous means dull and in one flat tone; it would bore an audience, not captivate it.
14256358.whyC: Vague means unclear; an unclear speech loses listeners instead of holding them.
14256358.whyD: Abrupt means sudden or curt; it describes how a speech ends or its tone, not why it captivates.
14256358.explanationTl: Ang 'eloquent' ay magaling at malinaw magsalita, kaya na-captivate ang audience. Yung ibang choices (monotonous, vague, abrupt) ay negative, kaya hindi sila tugma sa 'captivated'.
14256358.hintTl: Anong klaseng speech ang gugustuhin mong pakinggan hanggang dulo?

637573758.text: Fill in the blank: The horse jumped _____ the fence without touching it.
637573758.explanation: 'Over' shows movement from one side of something to the other, passing above it. 'Without touching it' rules out 'on', which means landing on the fence's surface.
637573758.hint: The horse never touched the fence. Which preposition means passing above something to the other side?
637573758.whyA: 'On' means landing on the surface of the fence, which contradicts 'without touching it'.
637573758.whyC: 'In' means inside something; you cannot jump inside a fence.
637573758.whyD: 'At' shows direction toward a target (jumped at someone), not clearing an obstacle.
637573758.explanationTl: Ang 'over' ay paglampas sa ibabaw papunta sa kabilang side. Dahil sabi 'without touching it', hindi pwede ang 'on' kasi ibig sabihin nun lumapag siya sa fence.
637573758.hintTl: Hindi tinamaan ng kabayo ang fence. Anong preposition ang ibig sabihin ay lumampas sa ibabaw?

800041561.hint: 'News' ends in -s, but is it really plural?
800041561.whyA: 'The' is the correct article here; nothing is wrong with it.
800041561.whyB: 'News' is the correct noun; the problem is the verb that agrees with it.
800041561.whyD: 'Good' is a correct predicate adjective after a linking verb.
800041561.explanationTl: Kahit may -s sa dulo, ang 'news' ay singular (uncountable noun). Kaya dapat 'The news is good', hindi 'are'.
800041561.hintTl: May -s ang 'news', pero plural ba talaga siya?

838470859.hint: Ownership with 'belong' always uses the same preposition: belong ___ someone.
838470859.whyB: 'Belong with' means fitting in a group or place (that cup belongs with the set), not ownership.
838470859.whyC: 'For' is a common Filipino-English slip; 'belong for' is not standard English.
838470859.whyD: 'Of' shows possession in phrases like 'the book of John', but 'belong' does not take 'of'.
838470859.explanationTl: Ang tamang idiom ay 'belong to' kapag pagmamay-ari. 'The book belongs to her' = kanya ang libro.
838470859.hintTl: Pag ownership, laging 'belong ___ someone'. Anong preposition yun?

904422609.text: Identify the error: 'Each of the players play well.'
904422609.explanation: The subject is 'Each', which is always singular; 'of the players' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'plays'.
904422609.hint: Find the real subject first. Is it 'Each' or 'players'?
904422609.whyA: 'Each' is correct; it is the singular subject the verb must agree with.
904422609.whyB: 'Players' is correctly plural inside the phrase 'of the players'; it is not the subject.
904422609.whyD: 'Well' is the correct adverb for the verb 'play'; 'good' would be the mistake.
904422609.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'Each', at laging singular yan. Yung 'of the players' ay prepositional phrase lang, hindi siya ang subject. Kaya dapat 'Each of the players plays well.'
904422609.hintTl: Hanapin muna ang totoong subject. 'Each' ba o 'players'?

986518591.hint: Some nouns name one object but are always plural, like 'pants' and 'eyeglasses'.
986518591.whyA: 'The' is the correct article; nothing is wrong with it.
986518591.whyB: 'Scissors' is the correct form; 'scissor' as a noun for the tool is not standard.
986518591.explanationTl: Ang 'scissors' ay laging plural, tulad ng 'pants' at 'eyeglasses'. Kaya dapat 'The scissors are sharp.'
986518591.hintTl: May mga noun na isang bagay lang pero laging plural, tulad ng 'pants'.

1106854031.hint: Look for the helping verb that points to something that has not happened yet.
1106854031.whyA: 'She eats' is simple present, for habits or general facts.
1106854031.whyB: 'She ate' is simple past; the action is already done.
1106854031.whyD: 'She is eating' is present progressive, an action happening right now.
1106854031.explanationTl: Ang 'will + base verb' ay simple future tense. Ang 'will eat' ay kakain pa lang siya.
1106854031.hintTl: Hanapin ang helping verb na nagsasabing mangyayari pa lang.

1365006955.text: Identify the error: 'Every member of the jury have voted.'
1365006955.explanation: The subject is 'member', made singular by 'Every'; 'of the jury' is only a prepositional phrase. The verb must be 'has voted'.
1365006955.hint: What is the head noun of the subject, and is it singular or plural?
1365006955.whyA: 'Every' is correct; it is what makes the subject singular.
1365006955.whyB: 'Member' is correctly singular after 'Every'; 'members' would be wrong.
1365006955.whyD: 'Voted' is the correct past participle; only the helping verb is wrong.
1365006955.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'member', at singular siya dahil sa 'Every'. Yung 'of the jury' ay phrase lang. Kaya dapat 'Every member of the jury has voted.'
1365006955.hintTl: Ano ang main noun ng subject? Singular ba o plural?

1444166743.hint: Ignore 'of the decision'. What is the real subject?
1444166743.whyA: 'Were' is plural; the subject 'impact' is singular.
1444166743.whyC: 'Are' is plural and also present tense; the subject 'impact' is singular.
1444166743.whyD: 'Have significant' is ungrammatical; 'significant' is an adjective and needs a linking verb like 'was'.
1444166743.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'impact' (singular), hindi 'decision'. Kaya singular verb: 'The impact of the decision was significant.'
1444166743.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the decision'. Ano ang totoong subject?

1562931377.hint: Ignore 'of the experiment'. Is the real subject singular or plural?
1562931377.whyA: 'Was' agrees with 'experiment', the noun closest to the blank, but the subject is 'results'.
1562931377.whyC: 'Is' is singular; the subject 'results' is plural.
1562931377.whyD: 'Has surprising' is ungrammatical; an adjective needs a linking verb, and 'has' is singular anyway.
1562931377.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'results' (plural), hindi 'experiment'. Kaya plural verb: 'The results of the experiment were surprising.'
1562931377.hintTl: Huwag pansinin ang 'of the experiment'. Singular ba o plural ang totoong subject?

1142168602.explanation: A basic English sentence follows article + noun (subject), then the linking verb, then the adjective: 'The flowers are beautiful.'
1142168602.hint: Start with the subject (article + noun), then the verb.
1142168602.whyA: It puts the adjective 'beautiful' in the subject slot and the noun after the verb, so the sentence makes no sense.
1142168602.whyC: The verb 'are' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'flowers'.
1142168602.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
1142168602.explanationTl: Ang basic na ayos: article + noun (subject), tapos verb, tapos adjective. Kaya 'The flowers are beautiful.'
1142168602.hintTl: Unahin ang subject (article + noun), saka ang verb.

1691343255.explanation: The subject 'the cat' comes first, then the progressive verb 'is sleeping' (helping verb + present participle): 'The cat is sleeping.'
1691343255.hint: Keep the article with its noun, and keep 'is' right before 'sleeping'.
1691343255.whyA: It puts 'sleeping' in the subject slot and leaves 'cat' at the end with no role.
1691343255.whyC: The verb 'is' splits the article 'The' from its noun 'cat'.
1691343255.whyD: The article 'the' must come before its noun, not after it.
1691343255.explanationTl: Una ang subject na 'the cat', tapos ang verb na 'is sleeping' (helping verb + -ing). Kaya 'The cat is sleeping.'
1691343255.hintTl: Dapat magkasama ang article at noun, at 'is' bago ang 'sleeping'.

1965033272.text: What is implied by the sentence 'The movie was exciting, but the ending was predictable.'?
1965033272.optionB: The ending was less exciting than the rest of the movie.
1965033272.explanation: 'But' sets up a contrast: the movie overall was exciting, while the ending, being predictable, did not keep up that excitement.
1965033272.hint: What does the word 'but' contrast the ending with?
1965033272.whyA: Too strong: the sentence calls the movie exciting, so it does not say the movie was bad.
1965033272.whyC: Contradicts the sentence: a predictable ending is the opposite of a surprising one.
1965033272.whyD: Overgeneralizes: only the ending is called predictable; the rest was exciting.
1965033272.explanationTl: Ang 'but' ay nagpapakita ng contrast: exciting ang movie, pero predictable ang ending, kaya hindi kasing-exciting ang ending kumpara sa iba.
1965033272.hintTl: Ano ang kinokontra ng 'but' sa ending?

83162521.hint: A businessman described this way would be hard to fool.
83162521.whyA: Foolish is the opposite of astute.
83162521.whyC: Naive means inexperienced and easily fooled, the opposite of astute.
83162521.whyD: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, the opposite of astute.
83162521.explanationTl: Ang 'astute' ay matalino at magaling bumasa ng sitwasyon, parang 'shrewd' o wais. Ang ibang choices ay kabaligtaran.
83162521.hintTl: Ang ganitong businessman ay mahirap lokohin.

200646296.hint: Think of a long climb up a steep mountain.
200646296.whyA: Easy is the opposite of arduous.
200646296.whyC: Simple is the opposite of arduous.
200646296.whyD: Effortless is the opposite of arduous, which means needing great effort.
200646296.explanationTl: Ang 'arduous' ay mahirap at nakakapagod, kailangan ng matinding effort. Kaya 'difficult' ang sagot.
200646296.hintTl: Isipin ang pag-akyat sa matarik na bundok.

1464501749.hint: How would you feel facing this task before you even start?
1464501749.whyA: Easy is the opposite; a daunting task looks hard.
1464501749.whyC: Simple is the opposite; a daunting task looks complicated.
1464501749.whyD: Straightforward is the opposite; a daunting task looks overwhelming.
1464501749.explanationTl: Ang 'daunting' ay nakakatakot o nakakapanghina ng loob dahil mukhang mahirap. Kaya 'intimidating' ang sagot.
1464501749.hintTl: Ano ang pakiramdam mo bago mo pa simulan ang ganitong task?

1697800269.text:
The scientist examined the minute details of the cell.

In this sentence, 'minute' most nearly means:
1697800269.explanation: As an adjective (pronounced my-NOOT), 'minute' means extremely small; details of a cell are tiny. The time-unit meaning (MIN-it) is a noun and does not fit here.
1697800269.hint: Here 'minute' describes details. How big are the details of a single cell?
1697800269.whyB: That is the noun 'minute' (60 seconds); in this sentence the word is an adjective describing 'details'.
1697800269.whyC: Confuses 'minute' with doing something 'in a minute' (quickly); the word describes size, not speed.
1697800269.whyD: Details can be important, but 'minute' describes their size, not their importance.
1697800269.explanationTl: Dito, adjective ang 'minute' (basa: my-NOOT) at ang ibig sabihin ay napakaliit. Ang 'minute' na 60 seconds ay noun, kaya hindi bagay dito.
1697800269.hintTl: Inilalarawan ng 'minute' ang details. Gaano kalaki ang details ng isang cell?

35942117.text: Broom is to sweeping as needle is to:
35942117.explanation: A broom is the tool used for sweeping; a needle is the tool used for sewing. The pair is tool : the job it does.
35942117.hint: Ask: what job is this tool made to do?
35942117.whyB: Ironing uses a flat iron, not a needle.
35942117.whyC: Weaving is done on a loom by interlacing threads, not with a sewing needle.
35942117.whyD: Folding is done by hand; it is not a needle's job.
35942117.explanationTl: Ang broom ay ginagamit sa sweeping, at ang needle naman ay ginagamit sa sewing. Tool : ang ginagawa nito ang relationship.
35942117.hintTl: Tanungin mo: ano ang trabaho ng tool na 'to?

183168070.hint: Think of the main action each tool performs.
183168070.whyB: Nailing is the hammer's job, not the saw's.
183168070.whyC: Sanding is done with sandpaper or a sander.
183168070.whyD: Drilling is done with a drill.
183168070.explanationTl: Ang hammer ay pang-pound, ang saw naman ay pang-cut. Tool : action ang pattern.
183168070.hintTl: Isipin mo kung ano ang main na ginagawa ng bawat tool.

327417457.hint: Pair each quantity with its standard unit.
327417457.whyD: Newtons measure force (including weight), not mass.
327417457.explanationTl: Ang area ay sinusukat in square meters, at ang mass ay in kilograms. Quantity : unit ang relationship.
327417457.hintTl: I-match mo ang bawat quantity sa standard unit nito.

571070274.hint: Which option is a unit of time?
571070274.explanationTl: Ang angle ay sinusukat in degrees, ang time naman in seconds. Quantity : unit ulit ang pattern.
571070274.hintTl: Alin sa options ang unit ng time?

828334311.explanation: An odometer is the instrument that shows mileage; a compass is the instrument that shows direction. The pair is instrument : what it indicates.
828334311.hint: What reading does each instrument give you?
828334311.whyA: Speed is shown by a speedometer, not a compass.
828334311.whyB: Hiking is an activity where a compass may be used, not what it indicates.
828334311.whyC: The needle is a part of the compass, not what it indicates.
828334311.explanationTl: Ang odometer ay nagpapakita ng mileage, ang compass naman ay nagpapakita ng direction. Instrument : ang sinusukat nito.
828334311.hintTl: Anong reading ang binibigay ng bawat instrument?

1555712605.hint: What is a camera's basic job, the way measuring is a ruler's?
1555712605.whyB: Printing is done by a printer after the photo is taken, not by the camera.
1555712605.whyC: Lighting comes from a flash or lamp; it is not the camera's main purpose.
1555712605.whyD: Focusing is one step in using a camera, not what it is for.
1555712605.explanationTl: Ang ruler ay pang-measure, ang camera naman ay pang-photograph. Tool : main purpose nito.
1555712605.hintTl: Ano ang basic na trabaho ng camera, gaya ng pag-measure sa ruler?

1631256051.hint: Find the unit used for length or distance.
1631256051.explanationTl: Ang volume ay in liters, ang distance naman in meters. Quantity : unit.
1631256051.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang unit ng length o distance.

1707578260.hint: Recall the SI unit for the flow of electric charge.
1707578260.whyA: Volts measure voltage (potential difference), not current.
1707578260.explanationTl: Ang length ay in meters, ang electric current naman in amperes. Huwag malito sa volts (voltage), ohms (resistance) at watts (power).
1707578260.hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang SI unit ng electric current.

269705685.text: Statement: "To win the inter-school debate, our team must prepare its arguments early." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
269705685.optionA: Preparing early guarantees that the team will win.
269705685.optionB: The team wants to win the inter-school debate.
269705685.optionC: The other teams have not prepared at all.
269705685.optionD: Debates are judged only on how early teams prepare.
269705685.explanation: The speaker is planning how to win, so the statement takes for granted that the team wants to win. The other options claim more than the statement says.
269705685.hint: An assumption is something the speaker takes for granted; watch out for words like 'guarantees' and 'only'.
269705685.whyA: 'Must prepare' means preparing is needed, not that it guarantees a win.
269705685.whyC: The statement says nothing about the other teams.
269705685.whyD: 'Only' goes too far; early preparation can matter without being the sole basis of judging.
269705685.explanationTl: Nagpaplano ang speaker kung paano mananalo, kaya assumed na gusto talagang manalo ng team. Yung ibang options, sobra na sa sinasabi ng statement.
269705685.hintTl: Ang assumption ay yung tinatanggap na lang ng speaker na totoo; ingat sa mga salitang 'guarantees' at 'only'.

796708615.text: Statement: "To raise office morale, the new division chief plans to personally thank employees for good work." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
796708615.optionA: Being thanked can lift employees' morale.
796708615.optionB: Thanking employees is the only way to raise morale.
796708615.optionC: Office morale is already at its highest.
796708615.optionD: Employees care only about cash bonuses.
796708615.explanation: The chief would use thanks to raise morale only if thanking people can actually lift it, so that is the assumption. The other options overstate or contradict the plan.
796708615.hint: Ask: what must the chief believe for this plan to make sense?
796708615.whyB: 'Only way' overstates it; the plan needs thanks to help, not to be the sole method.
796708615.whyC: If morale were already at its highest, there would be no need to raise it, so this contradicts the statement.
796708615.whyD: If employees cared only about bonuses, thanking them would not work, so this goes against the plan.
796708615.explanationTl: Gagamitin lang ng chief ang pag-thank para tumaas ang morale kung naniniwala siyang nakakataas talaga ito ng morale. Yun ang assumption.
796708615.hintTl: Tanungin mo: ano ang dapat paniwalaan ng chief para may sense ang plan niya?

823971108.text: Statement: "Maria enrolled in a review center so that she can pass the Civil Service Exam." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
823971108.optionA: Maria has failed the Civil Service Exam before.
823971108.optionB: Review centers guarantee that every enrollee passes.
823971108.optionC: Studying on one's own never works.
823971108.optionD: A review center can help her prepare for the exam.
823971108.explanation: Maria enrolls in order to pass, so she must believe the review center can help her prepare. The other options are not needed for her decision to make sense.
823971108.hint: Look for the belief behind Maria's reason for enrolling, not an extreme claim.
823971108.whyA: The statement does not say whether she has taken the exam before.
823971108.whyB: 'Guarantee that every enrollee passes' is too strong; she only needs the review to help.
823971108.whyC: 'Never works' is too strong; she can choose a review center without believing self-study is useless.
823971108.explanationTl: Nag-enroll si Maria para pumasa, kaya naniniwala siya na makakatulong ang review center sa pag-prepare niya. Yun ang assumption.
823971108.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang paniniwala sa likod ng dahilan ni Maria, hindi yung extreme na claim.

985585971.text: Statement: "The company requires its new call-center agents to practise speaking English for one hour every day." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
985585971.optionA: The new agents already speak perfect English.
985585971.optionB: Every agent will become fluent within one month.
985585971.optionC: Daily speaking practice can improve the agents' English.
985585971.optionD: The agents will never need any other language at work.
985585971.explanation: The company requires the practice because it believes practice can improve the agents' English. The other options are either contradicted by the rule or not needed for it.
985585971.hint: Why would the company bother requiring the practice?
985585971.whyA: If they already spoke perfect English, the practice would be pointless, so this contradicts the rule.
985585971.whyB: The rule expects improvement, not a specific result within one month.
985585971.whyD: 'Never' goes too far; the rule only needs English to matter, not to be the only language used.
985585971.explanationTl: Nire-require ng company ang practice kasi naniniwala silang gagaling ang English ng agents dahil dito. Yun ang assumption.
985585971.hintTl: Bakit pa ire-require ng company ang practice?

105547188.explanation: Each number is coded as the square of the next number, (n + 1)^2, so 6 = 7^2 = 49.
105547188.hint: Look at the right-hand numbers: are they perfect squares?
105547188.explanationTl: Ang bawat number ay naging square ng kasunod na number, (n + 1)^2, kaya 6 = 7^2 = 49.
105547188.hintTl: Tingnan mo ang numbers sa kanan: perfect squares ba sila?
105547188.whyA: 48 is 7^2 - 1; it misses the perfect-square pattern by one.
105547188.whyC: 50 adds 14 to 36; the jumps are 9, 11, 13, so the next jump is 13, not 14.
105547188.whyD: 51 adds 15 to 36, skipping a step in the jumps 9, 11, 13.

587274041.steps:
1. Differences: 18 - 10 = 8, 28 - 18 = 10; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 12, so 28 + 12 = 40.
3. Check with n^2 + 3n: 5^2 + 3(5) = 25 + 15 = 40.
587274041.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
587274041.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 18 - 10 = 8, 28 - 18 = 10; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 12, kaya 28 + 12 = 40.
3. I-check: 5^2 + 3(5) = 25 + 15 = 40.
587274041.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
587274041.whyA: 38 adds 10 again; the differences grow by 2 (8, 10, 12).
587274041.whyB: 39 is one short; usually from using n^2 + 2n + 4, which does not fit 3 = 18.
587274041.whyD: 41 overshoots by one; the next difference is 12, not 13.

1695189728.explanation: The coded values go up by 9, then 11, so the next jump is 13: 31 + 13 = 44. The rule is n^2 + 4n - 1.
1695189728.steps:
1. Differences: 20 - 11 = 9, 31 - 20 = 11; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 13, so 31 + 13 = 44.
3. Check with n^2 + 4n - 1: 25 + 20 - 1 = 44.
1695189728.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
1695189728.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ng coded values ay 9, tapos 11, kaya ang susunod ay 13: 31 + 13 = 44. Ang rule ay n^2 + 4n - 1.
1695189728.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 20 - 11 = 9, 31 - 20 = 11; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 13, kaya 31 + 13 = 44.
3. I-check: 25 + 20 - 1 = 44.
1695189728.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
1695189728.whyB: 45 assumes n^2 + 3n + 5, which gives 15 for n = 2, not 11.
1695189728.whyC: 46 adds 15; the differences go 9, 11, 13, so the next is 13.
1695189728.whyD: 47 adds 16, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.

1966047099.hint: Try writing each coded value as a product of two consecutive numbers.
1966047099.explanationTl: Ang bawat number ay naging (n + 1)(n + 2): 3 x 4 = 12, 4 x 5 = 20, 5 x 6 = 30, kaya 5 = 6 x 7 = 42.
1966047099.hintTl: Subukan mong isulat ang bawat value bilang product ng dalawang magkasunod na numbers.
1966047099.whyB: 44 adds 14; the differences go 8, 10, 12, so the next is 12.
1966047099.whyC: 46 comes from the wrong rule n^2 + 3n + 6, which gives 16 for n = 2.
1966047099.whyD: 48 adds 18, far more than the next difference of 12.

2050284569.explanation: The coded values go up by 9, then 11, so the next jump is 13: 30 + 13 = 43. The rule is n^2 + 4n - 2.
2050284569.steps:
1. Differences: 19 - 10 = 9, 30 - 19 = 11; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 13, so 30 + 13 = 43.
3. Check with n^2 + 4n - 2: 25 + 20 - 2 = 43.
2050284569.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
2050284569.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ng coded values ay 9, tapos 11, kaya ang susunod ay 13: 30 + 13 = 43. Ang rule ay n^2 + 4n - 2.
2050284569.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 19 - 10 = 9, 30 - 19 = 11; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 13, kaya 30 + 13 = 43.
3. I-check: 25 + 20 - 2 = 43.
2050284569.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
2050284569.whyA: 42 adds 12; the differences go 9, 11, 13, so the next is 13.
2050284569.whyC: 44 comes from the rule n^2 + 3n + 4, which gives 14 for n = 2, not 10.
2050284569.whyD: 45 adds 15, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.

2069883621.steps:
1. Differences: 11 - 5 = 6, 19 - 11 = 8; they grow by 2.
2. Next difference = 10, so 19 + 10 = 29.
3. Check with n^2 + 3n + 1: 16 + 12 + 1 = 29.
2069883621.hint: Find the differences between the coded values and see how they change.
2069883621.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 11 - 5 = 6, 19 - 11 = 8; nadadagdagan ng 2.
2. Next difference = 10, kaya 19 + 10 = 29.
3. I-check: 16 + 12 + 1 = 29.
2069883621.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang differences ng coded values at tingnan kung paano sila nagbabago.
2069883621.whyA: 28 adds 9; the differences go 6, 8, 10, so the next is 10.
2069883621.whyC: 30 adds 11, overshooting the +2 growth in the differences.
2069883621.whyD: 31 adds 12, as if the differences grew by 4.

636588524.text: A graph shows the noon temperature in a town: Monday 15 °C, Tuesday 20 °C, Wednesday 25 °C. What is the average temperature for the three days?
636588524.steps:
1. Add the values: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.
2. Divide by the number of days: 60 / 3 = 20.
3. Average = 20 °C.
636588524.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.
636588524.whyA: 18 °C is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
636588524.whyD: 24 °C is close to the highest reading, not the average.
636588524.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 15 + 20 + 25 = 60.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng araw: 60 / 3 = 20.
3. Average = 20 °C.
636588524.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng values.

734611293.text: A graph shows the noon temperature in a city: Day 1 25 °C, Day 2 30 °C, Day 3 35 °C. What is the average temperature for the three days?
734611293.steps:
1. Add the values: 25 + 30 + 35 = 90.
2. Divide by the number of days: 90 / 3 = 30.
3. Average = 30 °C.
734611293.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many there are.
734611293.whyA: 28 °C is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
734611293.whyD: 34 °C is close to the highest reading, not the average.
734611293.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 25 + 30 + 35 = 90.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng araw: 90 / 3 = 30.
3. Average = 30 °C.
734611293.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng values.

763597739.text: A graph shows a factory's rice-sack production: Q1 500 sacks, Q2 550 sacks, Q3 600 sacks. What is the average production per quarter?
763597739.steps:
1. Add the values: 500 + 550 + 600 = 1,650.
2. Divide by the number of quarters: 1,650 / 3 = 550.
3. Average = 550 sacks.
763597739.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many quarters there are.
763597739.whyA: 540 is below the middle value; with evenly spaced values the average equals the middle one.
763597739.whyD: 570 leans toward the highest quarter instead of the average.
763597739.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang values: 500 + 550 + 600 = 1,650.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng quarters: 1,650 / 3 = 550.
3. Average = 550 sacks.
763597739.hintTl: I-add mo lahat, tapos i-divide sa dami ng quarters.

1429217809.text: A graph shows a store's monthly sales: January ₱100,000, February ₱150,000, March ₱120,000. What is the average monthly sales, rounded to the nearest peso?
1429217809.hint: Add all three months, then divide by 3.
1429217809.whyB: ₱120,000 is the middle (median) value, not the average.
1429217809.whyD: ₱125,000 is the midpoint of the lowest and highest months, ignoring March's value.
1429217809.explanationTl: Average = 370,000 / 3 = ₱123,333.33, o ₱123,333 kapag ni-round sa pinakamalapit na peso.
1429217809.hintTl: I-add mo ang tatlong buwan, tapos i-divide sa 3.

413502916.explanation: P is Q's father and Q is R's mother, so P is R's grandfather and R is P's grandchild.
413502916.steps:
1. P is Q's father: P is one generation above Q.
2. Q is R's mother: Q is one generation above R.
3. So P is two generations above R: R is P's grandchild.
413502916.hint: Count the generations from P down to R.
413502916.whyB: R is Q's child, not P's child.
413502916.whyC: Siblings share the same generation; R is two generations below P.
413502916.whyD: R is below P in the family line, not above.
413502916.explanationTl: Si P ang father ni Q, at si Q ang mother ni R. Kaya grandfather ni R si P, at grandchild ni P si R.
413502916.stepsTl:
1. Si P ang father ni Q: isang generation sa taas ni Q.
2. Si Q ang mother ni R: isang generation sa taas ni R.
3. Kaya dalawang generation ang layo: grandchild ni P si R.
413502916.hintTl: Bilangin mo ang generations mula kay P pababa kay R.

505467647.explanation: Q is a daughter of both P and R. P is Q's mother, so R is Q's father, which makes R P's husband.
505467647.steps:
1. P is Q's mother.
2. Q is R's daughter, so R is Q's other parent.
3. Q's mother is P, so R is Q's father.
4. Q's father is P's husband.
505467647.hint: Q has two parents; one of them is already named as the mother.
505467647.whyA: R is Q's parent, a generation above Q, so R cannot be P's son.
505467647.whyC: Q is the daughter; R is Q's parent.
505467647.whyD: R is Q's father, not P's father.
505467647.explanationTl: Si Q ay anak ni P at ni R. Mother si P, kaya father si R, at husband siya ni P.
505467647.stepsTl:
1. Si P ang mother ni Q.
2. Si Q ay daughter ni R, kaya si R ang isa pang parent ni Q.
3. Mother na si P, kaya father si R.
4. Ang father ni Q ay husband ni P.
505467647.hintTl: Dalawa ang parents ni Q; yung isa, na-mention na bilang mother.

887372409.explanation: F is the daughter of both E and G. E is F's father, so G is F's mother, which makes G E's wife.
887372409.steps:
1. E is F's father.
2. F is G's daughter, so G is F's other parent.
3. F's father is E, so G is F's mother.
4. F's mother is E's wife.
887372409.hint: F has two parents; one of them is already named as the father.
887372409.whyA: G is F's parent, a generation above F, and must be female, so not E's son.
887372409.whyC: F is the daughter; G is F's parent.
887372409.whyD: G is F's mother, not E's mother.
887372409.explanationTl: Si F ay anak ni E at ni G. Father si E, kaya mother si G, at wife siya ni E.
887372409.stepsTl:
1. Si E ang father ni F.
2. Si F ay daughter ni G, kaya si G ang isa pang parent ni F.
3. Father na si E, kaya mother si G.
4. Ang mother ni F ay wife ni E.
887372409.hintTl: Dalawa ang parents ni F; yung isa, na-mention na bilang father.

8810366.text: No poets are lazy. Some people are poets. Which conclusion follows?
8810366.explanation: The people who are poets cannot be lazy, since no poet is lazy. So at least some people are not lazy; nothing is known about the people who are not poets.
8810366.steps:
1. No poets are lazy.
2. Some people are poets.
3. Those people, being poets, are not lazy.
4. So some people are not lazy.
8810366.hint: Focus only on the people who are poets.
8810366.whyB: We know nothing about people who are not poets, so we cannot say no one is lazy.
8810366.whyC: This contradicts the premises: some people (the poets) are not lazy.
8810366.whyD: No poets are lazy, so no lazy person can be a poet.
8810366.explanationTl: Yung mga tao na poets, hindi lazy kasi walang poet na lazy. Kaya at least some people are not lazy; wala tayong alam sa mga hindi poets.
8810366.stepsTl:
1. Walang poet na lazy.
2. May mga tao na poets.
3. Yung mga yun, dahil poets, hindi lazy.
4. Kaya some people are not lazy.
8810366.hintTl: Mag-focus ka lang sa mga tao na poets.

104501795.text: All dogs bark. Spot barks. Which conclusion follows?
104501795.optionC: It cannot be determined whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.explanation: The premise says every dog barks, not that only dogs bark. Since other animals may bark too, Spot's barking does not tell us whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.steps:
1. All dogs bark: dogs are inside the group of barkers.
2. Spot is in the group of barkers.
3. The barkers may include non-dogs.
4. So we cannot tell whether Spot is a dog.
104501795.hint: Does 'all dogs bark' also mean 'only dogs bark'?
104501795.whyA: This reverses the premise (affirming the consequent); barking does not prove Spot is a dog.
104501795.whyB: Nothing rules out Spot being a dog; dogs bark too.
104501795.whyD: 'All dogs bark' does not mean only dogs bark; this reverses the premise.
104501795.explanationTl: Sabi ng premise, lahat ng dogs ay nagba-bark, pero hindi sinabi na dogs lang ang nagba-bark. Kaya hindi natin masasabi kung dog si Spot.
104501795.stepsTl:
1. All dogs bark: kasama ang dogs sa grupo ng nagba-bark.
2. Kasama si Spot sa nagba-bark.
3. Pwedeng may hindi dog sa grupong yun.
4. Kaya cannot be determined kung dog si Spot.
104501795.hintTl: Ang 'all dogs bark' ba ay pareho ng 'only dogs bark'?

733498225.explanation: Every tree grow, and some plants are trees, so at least those plants grow. We cannot say all or none.
733498225.steps:
1. All trees grow.
2. Some plants are trees.
3. Those plants therefore grow.
4. So some plants grow.
733498225.hint: Look only at the plants that are trees.
733498225.whyA: Only some plants are trees; the others may not grow.
733498225.whyC: This contradicts the premises: the plants that are trees do grow.
733498225.whyD: A definite conclusion does follow: the overlap guarantees 'some'.
733498225.explanationTl: Lahat ng trees ay nag-grow, at may mga plants na trees, kaya at least yung mga yun ay nag-grow. Hindi natin masasabing lahat o wala.
733498225.stepsTl:
1. All trees grow.
2. Some plants are trees.
3. Kaya yung mga plants na yun ay nag-grow.
4. Kaya some plants grow.
733498225.hintTl: Tingnan mo lang yung mga plants na trees.

812446768.explanation: Every bird have feathers, and some animals are birds, so at least those animals have feathers. We cannot say all or none.
812446768.steps:
1. All birds have feathers.
2. Some animals are birds.
3. Those animals therefore have feathers.
4. So some animals have feathers.
812446768.hint: Look only at the animals that are birds.
812446768.whyA: Only some animals are birds; the others may not have feathers.
812446768.whyC: This contradicts the premises: the animals that are birds do have feathers.
812446768.whyD: A definite conclusion does follow: the overlap guarantees 'some'.
812446768.explanationTl: Lahat ng birds ay may feathers, at may mga animals na birds, kaya at least yung mga yun ay may feathers. Hindi natin masasabing lahat o wala.
812446768.stepsTl:
1. All birds have feathers.
2. Some animals are birds.
3. Kaya yung mga animals na yun ay may feathers.
4. Kaya some animals have feathers.
812446768.hintTl: Tingnan mo lang yung mga animals na birds.

1114052581.text: All dogs are loyal. No cat is a dog. Which conclusion follows?
1114052581.optionD: Nothing definite follows about whether cats are loyal.
1114052581.explanation: The premises say dogs are loyal, but they say nothing about animals that are not dogs. Cats may or may not be loyal, so no definite conclusion about cats follows.
1114052581.steps:
1. All dogs are loyal: dogs sit inside the group of loyal animals.
2. No cat is a dog: cats are outside the dog group.
3. Cats could still be inside or outside the loyal group.
4. So nothing definite follows about cats.
1114052581.hint: Being outside the dog group does not tell you whether you are outside the loyal group.
1114052581.whyA: A common error: 'not a dog' does not mean 'not loyal'; other animals can be loyal too.
1114052581.whyB: Nothing in the premises says cats are loyal.
1114052581.whyC: This might be true, but it does not follow from the premises.
1114052581.explanationTl: Sinabi lang na loyal ang dogs; walang sinabi tungkol sa hindi dogs. Kaya hindi natin alam kung loyal ang cats o hindi.
1114052581.stepsTl:
1. All dogs are loyal: nasa loob ng loyal group ang dogs.
2. No cat is a dog: nasa labas ng dog group ang cats.
3. Pwedeng nasa loob o labas ng loyal group ang cats.
4. Kaya walang definite na conclusion tungkol sa cats.
1114052581.hintTl: Ang pagiging hindi dog ay hindi nangangahulugang hindi loyal.

1862564295.explanation: Every planet have orbits, and some celestial bodies are planets, so at least those celestial bodies have orbits. We cannot say all or none.
1862564295.steps:
1. All planets have orbits.
2. Some celestial bodies are planets.
3. Those celestial bodies therefore have orbits.
4. So some celestial bodies have orbits.
1862564295.hint: Look only at the celestial bodies that are planets.
1862564295.whyA: Only some celestial bodies are planets; the others may not have orbits.
1862564295.whyC: This contradicts the premises: the celestial bodies that are planets do have orbits.
1862564295.whyD: A definite conclusion does follow: the overlap guarantees 'some'.
1862564295.explanationTl: Lahat ng planets ay may orbit, at may mga celestial bodies na planets, kaya at least yung mga yun ay may orbit. Hindi natin masasabing lahat o wala.
1862564295.stepsTl:
1. All planets have orbits.
2. Some celestial bodies are planets.
3. Kaya yung mga celestial bodies na yun ay may orbit.
4. Kaya some celestial bodies have orbits.
1862564295.hintTl: Tingnan mo lang yung mga celestial bodies na planets.

364905136.text: Odd one out: Lion, Tiger, Elephant, Leopard
364905136.explanation: Lion, tiger and leopard are big cats that eat meat; the elephant is a plant-eater and not a cat.
364905136.hint: Three of these belong to the same animal family.
364905136.whyA: The lion is a meat-eating big cat, like the tiger and leopard.
364905136.whyB: The tiger is a meat-eating big cat, like the lion and leopard.
364905136.whyD: The leopard is a meat-eating big cat, like the lion and tiger.
364905136.explanationTl: Ang lion, tiger at leopard ay big cats na kumakain ng karne; ang elephant ay herbivore at hindi cat.
364905136.hintTl: Tatlo sa kanila ay galing sa iisang animal family.

466601111.text: Odd one out: Car, Jeepney, Motorcycle, Airplane
466601111.explanation: Car, jeepney and motorcycle are motor vehicles that travel on roads; the airplane travels by air.
466601111.hint: Think of where each vehicle travels.
466601111.whyA: A car is a road vehicle, like the jeepney and motorcycle.
466601111.whyB: A jeepney is a road vehicle, like the car and motorcycle.
466601111.whyC: A motorcycle is a road vehicle, like the car and jeepney.
466601111.explanationTl: Ang car, jeepney at motorcycle ay sa kalsada bumibiyahe; ang airplane ay sa himpapawid.
466601111.hintTl: Isipin mo kung saan bumibiyahe ang bawat sasakyan.

483963428.hint: How does each instrument make its sound?
483963428.whyA: The violin is a string instrument, like the guitar and harp.
483963428.whyB: The guitar is a string instrument, like the violin and harp.
483963428.whyD: The harp is a string instrument, like the violin and guitar.
483963428.explanationTl: Ang flute ay wind instrument (hinihipan), habang string instruments ang violin, guitar at harp.
483963428.hintTl: Paano lumalabas ang tunog ng bawat instrument?

1387829418.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how is the Speaker of the House of Representatives chosen?
1387829418.optionB: Elected by a majority vote of all the Members of the House
1387829418.optionC: Elected by the people in a nationwide vote
1387829418.optionD: The longest-serving Member automatically becomes Speaker
1387829418.explanation: Article VI, Section 16(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that the House of Representatives elects its Speaker by a majority vote of all its Members. The Senate elects its President the same way.
1387829418.hint: Each chamber of Congress picks its own presiding officer.
1387829418.whyA: The President has no power to appoint the leaders of Congress; that would violate separation of powers.
1387829418.whyC: Only the President, Vice-President and senators are elected nationwide; the Speaker is chosen by fellow Members.
1387829418.whyD: Seniority does not decide it; the Constitution requires an election by majority vote of all Members.
1387829418.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 16(1) ng 1987 Constitution, ang mga Members mismo ng House ang nag-e-elect ng Speaker, by majority vote of all Members. Ganun din sa Senate, sila ang pumipili ng Senate President.
1387829418.hintTl: Isipin mo: sino ang pumipili ng leader ng bawat chamber ng Congress?

2034682365.text: What is the main function of the Commission on Elections (COMELEC)?
2034682365.optionA: Enforce and administer all laws on the conduct of elections
2034682365.optionB: Audit the accounts of government agencies
2034682365.explanation: Under Article IX-C, Section 2(1) of the 1987 Constitution, the COMELEC enforces and administers all laws and regulations relating to the conduct of elections, plebiscites, initiatives, referendums and recalls.
2034682365.hint: The answer is in the commission's name.
2034682365.whyB: Auditing government accounts is the job of the Commission on Audit (Art. IX-D).
2034682365.whyC: Appointments belong mainly to the President; the Civil Service Commission handles the civil service, not COMELEC.
2034682365.whyD: Making laws is the job of Congress (Art. VI), not a constitutional commission.
2034682365.explanationTl: Sa Article IX-C, Section 2(1) ng 1987 Constitution, ang COMELEC ang nag-e-enforce at nag-a-administer ng lahat ng election laws, pati plebiscite, initiative, referendum at recall.
2034682365.hintTl: Nasa pangalan na mismo ng commission ang sagot.

1489601512.explanation: Section 7(d) of RA 6713 prohibits public officials and employees from soliciting or accepting gifts or anything of monetary value in connection with any transaction affected by the functions of their office. Political neutrality, professionalism and responsiveness are norms of conduct required under Section 4, not prohibited acts.
1489601512.hint: Three of the options are duties every public servant must follow.
1489601512.whyA: Political neutrality is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(h), not a prohibited act.
1489601512.whyC: Professionalism is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(b).
1489601512.whyD: Responsiveness to the public is a required norm of conduct under Section 4(e).
1489601512.explanationTl: Sa Section 7(d) ng RA 6713, bawal sa public officials at employees ang humingi o tumanggap ng regalo o anumang may halaga na konektado sa trabaho nila. Yung political neutrality, professionalism at responsiveness ay mga norms of conduct sa Section 4, ibig sabihin required yun, hindi bawal.
1489601512.hintTl: Tatlo sa choices ay mga dapat gawin ng public servant. Alin ang hindi?

160158279.hint: It is not Canada's biggest city; it sits in the province of Ontario on the border with Quebec.
160158279.whyA: Toronto is Canada's largest city, but not its capital.
160158279.whyC: Vancouver is a major west-coast city in British Columbia, not the capital.
160158279.whyD: Montreal is the largest city in Quebec, not the national capital.
160158279.explanationTl: Ottawa ang capital ng Canada, dito nakatayo ang Parliament nila. Madalas mapagkamalan ang Toronto kasi yun ang pinakamalaking city.
160158279.hintTl: Hindi ito ang pinakamalaking city ng Canada.

300226883.text: The Suez Canal, which links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, is located in which country?
300226883.explanation: The Suez Canal runs through Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea. It opened in 1869 and lets ships travel between Europe and Asia without sailing around Africa.
300226883.hint: Think of the country that lies between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, at the corner of Africa and Asia.
300226883.whyA: Sudan borders the Red Sea but not the Mediterranean, so the canal cannot be there.
300226883.whyC: Libya is on the Mediterranean but has no Red Sea coast.
300226883.whyD: Morocco is at the far western end of North Africa, near the Strait of Gibraltar.
300226883.explanationTl: Nasa Egypt ang Suez Canal, kinokonekta nito ang Mediterranean Sea at Red Sea. Binuksan ito noong 1869, kaya hindi na kailangang umikot ng barko sa buong Africa para makarating ng Asia mula Europe.
300226883.hintTl: Aling bansa ang nasa pagitan ng Mediterranean at Red Sea?

317658505.explanation: The blue whale is the largest mammal, and the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching about 30 meters (about 100 feet) in length.
317658505.hint: The biggest mammal does not live on land.
317658505.whyB: The elephant is the largest LAND animal, but it is far smaller than the blue whale.
317658505.whyC: The giraffe is the tallest animal, not the largest.
317658505.whyD: The rhinoceros is large but smaller than both the elephant and the blue whale.
317658505.explanationTl: Ang blue whale ang pinakamalaking mammal, at pinakamalaking hayop na nabuhay kailanman, umaabot ng mga 30 meters ang haba.
317658505.hintTl: Hindi sa lupa nakatira ang pinakamalaking mammal.

369340607.text: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
369340607.explanation: Albert Einstein developed the special theory of relativity (1905) and the general theory of relativity (1915), which changed how science understands space, time and gravity.
369340607.hint: His famous equation is E = mc².
369340607.whyA: Isaac Newton gave the laws of motion and universal gravitation, which relativity later refined.
369340607.whyC: Galileo pioneered experiments and the telescope, centuries before relativity.
369340607.whyD: Niels Bohr is known for his model of the atom and quantum theory, not relativity.
369340607.explanationTl: Si Albert Einstein ang nag-develop ng theory of relativity, yung special relativity noong 1905 at general relativity noong 1915. Binago nito ang pagkaintindi natin sa space, time at gravity.
369340607.hintTl: Siya yung may sikat na equation na E = mc².

608952765.hint: The nickname came from Europeans who knew little about this continent's interior.
608952765.whyA: Asia was well known to European traders and was never given this nickname.
608952765.whyC: South America is sometimes linked to the Amazon jungle, but it was not called the 'Dark Continent'.
608952765.whyD: Australia is sometimes called the 'Island Continent' or 'Land Down Under', not the 'Dark Continent'.
608952765.explanationTl: Africa ang tinawag na 'Dark Continent' noon kasi halos hindi pa na-e-explore ng mga Europeo ang loob nito, hindi dahil sa kulay ng mga tao.
608952765.hintTl: Galing ang nickname sa mga Europeo na halos walang alam sa loob ng kontinenteng ito.

657782264.hint: It is also the smallest planet and is named after the Roman messenger god.
657782264.whyA: Venus is the second planet from the Sun (and the hottest), not the closest.
657782264.whyC: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
657782264.whyD: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.
657782264.explanationTl: Mercury ang pinakamalapit na planet sa Sun, mga 58 million kilometers ang layo. Second ang Venus, third ang Earth.
657782264.hintTl: Ito rin ang pinakamaliit na planet.

1072534553.hint: Brazil was a Portuguese colony, and its currency has a Portuguese name meaning 'royal'.
1072534553.whyA: The peso is used by Spanish-speaking neighbours like Argentina and Chile (and by the Philippines), not Brazil.
1072534553.whyC: The dollar is used by the US and others, not Brazil.
1072534553.whyD: The euro is the currency of many European Union countries, not Brazil.
1072534553.explanationTl: Real ang official currency ng Brazil. Peso ang gamit ng mga kapitbahay nilang Spanish-speaking tulad ng Argentina at Chile, pero Portuguese-speaking ang Brazil.
1072534553.hintTl: Portuguese ang language ng Brazil, at Portuguese din ang pangalan ng pera nila.

1509638371.hint: This continent is also a single country.
1509638371.whyB: Europe is the second smallest continent, about 10 million square kilometers.
1509638371.whyC: Antarctica is about 14 million square kilometers, bigger than both Europe and Australia.
1509638371.whyD: South America is about 17.8 million square kilometers, much larger.
1509638371.explanationTl: Australia ang pinakamaliit na continent, mga 7.7 million square kilometers. Second smallest ang Europe.
1509638371.hintTl: Ang continent na ito ay isang bansa lang din.

1521342287.hint: The UK kept its own currency and never adopted the currency of the eurozone.
1521342287.whyA: The UK never adopted the euro, even while it was an EU member.
1521342287.whyC: The dollar is used by the US, Canada, Australia and others, not the UK.
1521342287.whyD: The yen is the currency of Japan.
1521342287.explanationTl: Pound Sterling ang official currency ng United Kingdom. Hindi sila nag-adopt ng euro kahit noong member pa sila ng EU.
1521342287.hintTl: Hindi nag-euro ang UK, may sarili silang pera.

1593956969.hint: He was an Italian Renaissance artist and inventor who also painted 'The Last Supper'.
1593956969.whyA: Van Gogh was a 19th-century Dutch painter known for 'The Starry Night'.
1593956969.whyC: Picasso was a 20th-century Spanish painter known for Cubism and 'Guernica'.
1593956969.whyD: Michelangelo was a Renaissance artist too, but he is known for the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the statue of David.
1593956969.explanationTl: Si Leonardo da Vinci ang nagpinta ng Mona Lisa, isang sikat na Renaissance painting. Si Michelangelo naman ang sa Sistine Chapel, kaya madalas silang napagpapalit.
1593956969.hintTl: Siya rin ang nagpinta ng 'The Last Supper'.

1708134427.text: Republic Act No. 9262 is also known as the:
1708134427.optionA: Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004
1708134427.explanation: RA 9262 is the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004 (Anti-VAWC Act), which defines and penalizes violence against women and their children.
1708134427.whyB: The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act is RA 3019.
1708134427.whyC: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act is RA 9003.
1708134427.whyD: The Labor Code is Presidential Decree No. 442, not a Republic Act.
1708134427.explanationTl: Ang RA 9262 ay ang Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004, o mas kilala bilang Anti-VAWC Act. Pinoprotektahan nito ang mga babae at mga anak nila laban sa violence.
1708134427.hintTl: Ang kilalang short name nito ay 'VAWC'.

1854968706.hint: He was a German astronomer who used Tycho Brahe's observations to show that orbits are ellipses.
1854968706.whyA: Newton later explained WHY Kepler's laws work using his law of universal gravitation.
1854968706.whyC: Galileo supported the Sun-centered model with telescope observations but did not formulate the laws of planetary motion.
1854968706.whyD: Copernicus proposed the Sun-centered (heliocentric) model, but with circular orbits; the laws came from Kepler.
1854968706.explanationTl: Si Johannes Kepler ang nag-formulate ng three laws of planetary motion noong early 1600s, kasama na yung elliptical ang orbit ng mga planeta. Si Newton ang nagpaliwanag kung bakit gumagana ang mga ito gamit ang gravity.
1854968706.hintTl: Siya ang nagsabing ellipse, hindi perfect circle, ang orbit ng mga planeta.

2055236491.explanation: France uses the euro. It adopted the euro in 1999, and euro banknotes and coins replaced the French franc in 2002.
2055236491.hint: France belongs to the eurozone of the European Union.
2055236491.whyA: The franc was France's currency before it was replaced by the euro.
2055236491.whyC: The pound is the currency of the United Kingdom.
2055236491.whyD: The dollar is used by the US and others, not France.
2055236491.explanationTl: Euro ang currency ng France ngayon. In-adopt nila ito noong 1999, at noong 2002 pinalitan na ng euro bills at coins ang lumang French franc.
2055236491.hintTl: Ang franc ay dati nilang pera. Ano ang pumalit?

2101546851.hint: It is the same gas we breathe out and plants take in.
2101546851.whyA: Nitrogen is used in some beers and coffee for a creamy foam, but soda's fizz comes from another gas.
2101546851.whyC: Oxygen is not what is dissolved in soft drinks to make them fizz.
2101546851.whyD: Helium is used in balloons, not drinks.
2101546851.explanationTl: Carbon dioxide ang naka-dissolve sa soda under pressure. Pagbukas mo ng bote, lumalabas ito bilang bubbles, kaya may fizz.
2101546851.hintTl: Ito yung gas na nilalabas natin pag huminga tayo.

190778579.explanation: The barong Tagalog, an embroidered shirt often made of piña or jusi fabric and worn untucked, is the recognized national costume for Filipino men.
190778579.hint: It is the embroidered formal shirt men wear to weddings and official events.
190778579.whyB: The baro't saya is the traditional national costume for Filipino WOMEN.
190778579.whyC: The malong is a tube-shaped wraparound cloth of Mindanao, worn by both men and women; it is not the national costume.
190778579.whyD: The salakot is a traditional wide-brimmed hat, not a costume.
190778579.explanationTl: Ang barong Tagalog ang kinikilalang national costume ng mga lalaking Pilipino. Embroidered na polo ito, madalas gawa sa piña o jusi, at hindi naka-tuck in.
190778579.hintTl: Ito yung sinusuot ng mga lalaki sa kasal at formal events.

924282981.explanation: Manila is the capital of the Philippines under Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976). Quezon City was the official capital from 1948 to 1976.
924282981.hint: One option was a former capital; the current one is the historic city along the Pasig River.
924282981.whyB: Cebu City is the oldest Spanish settlement and a major city, but not the capital.
924282981.whyC: Davao City is the biggest city in Mindanao, but not the capital.
924282981.whyD: Quezon City was the capital from 1948 to 1976, until PD 940 restored Manila.
924282981.explanationTl: Manila ang capital ng Pilipinas, ayon sa Presidential Decree No. 940 noong 1976. Ang Quezon City ay naging capital mula 1948 hanggang 1976, kaya madalas yun ang trap.
924282981.hintTl: Isa sa choices ay dating capital lang. Alin ang capital ngayon?

1513413537.hint: This hero lost the use of his legs to polio but became Aguinaldo's chief adviser.
1513413537.whyA: Jose Rizal is the national hero, known for 'Noli Me Tangere' and 'El Filibusterismo'.
1513413537.whyC: Andres Bonifacio is the 'Father of the Philippine Revolution' and founder of the Katipunan.
1513413537.whyD: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippine Republic; Mabini was his adviser.
1513413537.explanationTl: Si Apolinario Mabini ang 'Sublime Paralytic'. Naparalisa siya dahil sa polio, pero siya ang utak sa likod ng revolutionary government ni Aguinaldo, kaya tinawag din siyang 'Brains of the Revolution'.
1513413537.hintTl: Naparalisa siya pero naging chief adviser ni Aguinaldo.

1543417124.text: Which Philippine folk dance is performed while balancing lighted oil lamps on the head and the backs of the hands?
1543417124.explanation: Pandanggo sa Ilaw, from Mindoro, is danced while balancing three oil lamps (tinghoy), one on the head and one on the back of each hand. 'Ilaw' means light.
1543417124.hint: This dance comes from Mindoro and is a version of the fandango.
1543417124.whyA: Tinikling is danced between two clapping bamboo poles, imitating the tikling bird.
1543417124.whyB: Cariñosa is a flirtatious courtship dance done with a fan and handkerchief.
1543417124.whyD: Singkil is a Maranao royal dance done with fans while stepping between crisscrossed bamboo poles.
1543417124.explanationTl: Ang Pandanggo sa Ilaw, galing Mindoro, ay sinasayaw habang may binabalanse na tatlong oil lamp o tinghoy: isa sa ulo at tig-isa sa likod ng kamay. Ang 'ilaw' ay light.
1543417124.hintTl: Galing Mindoro ang sayaw na ito, at version siya ng fandango.

172219452.steps:
1. Substitute f = 20 and g = 8: e = 20 − 8.
2. Subtract: e = 12.
172219452.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang f = 20 at g = 8: e = 20 − 8.
2. I-subtract: e = 12.
172219452.explanation: Substitute the values: e = f − g = 20 − 8 = 12.
172219452.whyB: 28 is f + g; you added instead of subtracting.
172219452.whyC: 10 is a subtraction slip; 20 − 8 is 12, not 10.
172219452.whyD: 16 is 2 × g; you doubled g instead of subtracting it from f.

207501616.text: If b = c × d and c = 7, d = 3, what is b?
207501616.explanation: Substitute the values: b = c × d = 7 × 3 = 21.
207501616.steps:
1. Substitute c = 7 and d = 3: b = 7 × 3.
2. Multiply: b = 21.
207501616.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang c = 7 at d = 3: b = 7 × 3.
2. I-multiply: b = 21.
207501616.whyB: 10 is 7 + 3; you added instead of multiplying.
207501616.whyC: 4 is 7 − 3; you subtracted instead of multiplying.
207501616.whyD: 24 is 8 × 3; a multiplication slip, since 7 × 3 is 21.

612824269.hint: x is being multiplied by 8. What operation undoes multiplication?
612824269.hintTl: Naka-multiply ang x sa 8. Ano ang kabaligtaran ng multiplication?
612824269.steps:
1. Divide both sides by 8: x = 64 ÷ 8.
2. x = 8.
3. Check: 8 × 8 = 64 ✓
612824269.stepsTl:
1. I-divide ang both sides sa 8: x = 64 ÷ 8.
2. x = 8.
3. I-check: 8 × 8 = 64 ✓
612824269.explanationTl: I-divide ang both sides sa 8, kaya x = 64 ÷ 8 = 8.

389516047.text: What is 1/3 written as a decimal?
389516047.explanation: A fraction means numerator ÷ denominator: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333..., with the 3 repeating forever.
389516047.explanationTl: Ang fraction ay numerator ÷ denominator: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333..., paulit-ulit ang 3.
389516047.steps:
1. Divide the numerator by the denominator: 1 ÷ 3.
2. 3 goes into 10 three times with remainder 1, again and again.
3. 1/3 = 0.333...
389516047.stepsTl:
1. I-divide ang numerator sa denominator: 1 ÷ 3.
2. Ang 3 sa 10 ay 3 beses, may tirang 1, paulit-ulit.
3. 1/3 = 0.333...
389516047.hint: Divide the top number by the bottom number.
389516047.hintTl: I-divide ang nasa itaas sa nasa ibaba.

466426449.text: A regular hexagon has sides of 8 cm each. What is its perimeter?
466426449.explanation: A hexagon has 6 equal sides, so the perimeter is 6 × 8 cm = 48 cm.
466426449.explanationTl: Ang hexagon ay may 6 na sides, kaya ang perimeter ay 6 × 8 cm = 48 cm.
466426449.steps:
1. A hexagon has 6 sides.
2. Perimeter = number of sides × side length.
3. 6 × 8 cm = 48 cm.
466426449.stepsTl:
1. Ang hexagon ay may 6 na sides.
2. Perimeter = bilang ng sides × haba ng isang side.
3. 6 × 8 cm = 48 cm.
466426449.hint: Perimeter is the total length around the shape. Count how many sides a hexagon has.
466426449.hintTl: Ang perimeter ay kabuuang haba sa paligid. Ilan ba ang sides ng hexagon?

605251264.text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a heptagon (7 sides)?
605251264.explanation: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°, so a heptagon has (7 − 2) × 180° = 900°.
605251264.explanationTl: Ang sum ng interior angles ng polygon ay (n − 2) × 180°. Sa heptagon: (7 − 2) × 180° = 900°.
605251264.stepsTl:
1. Gamitin ang formula: sum = (n − 2) × 180°.
2. n = 7, kaya n − 2 = 5.
3. 5 × 180° = 900°.
605251264.hint: A polygon can be split into triangles from one corner; count the triangles.
605251264.hintTl: Puwedeng hatiin ang polygon sa mga triangle mula sa isang corner. Ilan ang triangles?
605251264.whyD: 1,260° is 7 × 180°; you forgot to subtract 2 from the number of sides.

98467538.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
98467538.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.

411712212.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
411712212.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.

1059750230.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
1059750230.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.

1752148487.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
1752148487.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.
1752148487.whyB: 35 is a division slip: 25% is one quarter, and 160 ÷ 4 = 40.

2021100914.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
2021100914.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.
2021100914.whyB: 15 is only 10% of 150; you still need to add 2% (which is 3).
2021100914.whyC: 20 is too big: 10% is 15 and 2% is 3, so 12% is 15 + 3 = 18.
2021100914.whyD: 12 just repeats the percent number; 12% of 150 is 18.

2097167053.hint: “Percent” means “out of 100”. Change the % to a decimal or a simple fraction, then multiply.
2097167053.hintTl: Ang “percent” ay “sa bawat 100”. Gawing decimal o fraction muna, tapos i-multiply.

539613295.text: A cyclist rides 30 km in 1 hour 30 minutes. What is the average speed in km/h?
539613295.explanation: 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours, so speed = 30 km ÷ 1.5 h = 20 km/h.
539613295.explanationTl: Ang 1 hour 30 minutes ay 1.5 hours. Speed = 30 ÷ 1.5 = 20 km/h.
539613295.steps:
1. Convert time to hours: 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h.
2. Speed = distance ÷ time = 30 km ÷ 1.5 h.
3. Speed = 20 km/h.
539613295.stepsTl:
1. Gawing hours ang oras: 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h.
2. Speed = distance ÷ time = 30 ÷ 1.5.
3. Speed = 20 km/h.
539613295.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time, with the time written in hours.
539613295.hintTl: Bilis = layo ÷ oras. Siguraduhing nasa hours ang oras.
539613295.whyB: 45 is 30 × 1.5; you multiplied instead of dividing.
539613295.whyC: 30 ignores the extra 30 minutes and divides by 1 hour only.
539613295.whyD: 15 divides by 2 hours; 1 h 30 min is 1.5 h, not 2 h.

1446253096.steps:
1. Convert time to hours: 45 min = 45/60 = 0.75 h.
2. Speed = distance ÷ time = 60 km ÷ 0.75 h.
3. Speed = 80 km/h.
1446253096.stepsTl:
1. Gawing hours ang oras: 45 min = 45/60 = 0.75 h.
2. Speed = 60 ÷ 0.75.
3. Speed = 80 km/h.
1446253096.explanation: 45 minutes = 0.75 hour, so speed = 60 km ÷ 0.75 h = 80 km/h.
1446253096.explanationTl: Ang 45 minutes ay 0.75 hour, kaya 60 ÷ 0.75 = 80 km/h.
1446253096.whyB: At 90 km/h the train would cover 67.5 km in 45 minutes, not 60 km.
1446253096.whyC: At 70 km/h the train would cover only 52.5 km in 45 minutes.
1446253096.whyD: 100 km/h comes from treating 45 minutes as 0.6 hour; 45 minutes is 0.75 hour.

277354909.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, ?
277354909.explanation: The terms are cubes: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³. The next is 6³ = 216.
277354909.explanationTl: Cubes ang mga numero: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³. Kaya ang susunod ay 6³ = 216.
277354909.hint: Each term is a whole number multiplied by itself more than once.
277354909.hintTl: Bawat term ay isang number na minultiply sa sarili niya nang ilang beses.
277354909.whyB: 150 adds 25, but the gaps (7, 19, 37, 61) keep growing, so the next gap is 91.
277354909.whyC: 100 is smaller than 125; the sequence is increasing.
277354909.whyD: 175 adds 50; the next gap is 91, not 50.

1260676570.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, ?
1260676570.explanation: Each term is 4 more than the one before: 17 + 4 = 21.
1260676570.whyD: 15 goes down, but the sequence increases by 4.

1570412187.explanation: Each term is 3 times the one before: 81 × 3 = 243.
1570412187.whyC: 108 is 81 + 27; the pattern multiplies, it does not add the previous term.

1677984835.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 7, 14, 28, 56, ?
1677984835.explanation: Each term is double the one before: 56 × 2 = 112.
1677984835.whyB: 84 is 56 + 28; the pattern doubles, it does not add the previous term.
1677984835.whyC: 70 is 56 + 14; the pattern doubles each term.
1677984835.whyD: 98 is 56 + 42; the gaps double too (7, 14, 28), so the next gap is 56.

1911138141.explanation: The terms are squares going down: 7², 6², 5², 4², so the next is 3² = 9.
1911138141.explanationTl: Squares ito na pababa: 7², 6², 5², 4², kaya ang susunod ay 3² = 9.
1911138141.steps:
1. 49 = 7², 36 = 6², 25 = 5², 16 = 4².
2. Next: 3² = 9.
3. Check with gaps: −13, −11, −9, so the next gap is −7, and 16 − 7 = 9.
1911138141.stepsTl:
1. 49 = 7², 36 = 6², 25 = 5², 16 = 4².
2. Susunod: 3² = 9.
3. I-check sa gaps: −13, −11, −9, kaya ang next gap ay −7, at 16 − 7 = 9.
1911138141.whyB: 4 is 2²; it skips 3² and comes one step too far.
1911138141.whyD: 7 is the size of the next gap, not the next term; 16 − 7 = 9.

2022239685.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ?
2022239685.explanation: Each term is 5 more than the one before: 25 + 5 = 30.
2022239685.whyB: 50 doubles 25; the pattern adds 5 each time.

53623703.text: A barangay sports fest has 6 soccer teams. Each team has 11 players on the field and 5 substitutes. How many players are there in all?
53623703.explanation: Each team has 11 + 5 = 16 players, so 6 teams have 6 × 16 = 96 players.
53623703.explanationTl: Bawat team ay may 11 + 5 = 16 players. Sa 6 teams: 6 × 16 = 96.
53623703.hint: Find how many players ONE team has first.
53623703.hintTl: Alamin muna kung ilan ang players ng ISANG team.
53623703.whyA: 66 counts only the 11 players on the field and forgets the substitutes.
53623703.whyB: 71 is 6 × 11 + 5; the 5 substitutes are per team, not for the whole fest.

1111574015.text: Lito saves ₱75 every week. Counting a year as 52 weeks, how much does he save in one year?
1111574015.steps:
1. Total = weekly savings × number of weeks.
2. ₱75 × 52 = ₱75 × 50 + ₱75 × 2 = ₱3,750 + ₱150.
3. Total = ₱3,900.
1111574015.stepsTl:
1. Total = ipon kada linggo × bilang ng linggo.
2. ₱75 × 52 = ₱75 × 50 + ₱75 × 2 = ₱3,750 + ₱150.
3. Total = ₱3,900.
1111574015.hint: Multiply the weekly amount by the number of weeks. Break 52 into 50 + 2 to make it easy.
1111574015.hintTl: I-multiply ang weekly na ipon sa bilang ng weeks. Hatiin ang 52 sa 50 + 2 para madali.
1111574015.whyA: ₱3,600 uses 48 weeks (4 weeks × 12 months); the stem says 52 weeks.
1111574015.whyC: ₱900 is ₱75 × 12, as if he saved once a month.

1407941946.text: A music teacher restrings 9 six-string guitars and 4 four-string bass guitars. How many strings does she need in all?
1407941946.explanation: 9 × 6 = 54 strings for the guitars and 4 × 4 = 16 for the basses, so 54 + 16 = 70 strings.
1407941946.explanationTl: 9 × 6 = 54 para sa guitars, 4 × 4 = 16 para sa bass. Total: 54 + 16 = 70 strings.
1407941946.steps:
1. Guitars: 9 × 6 = 54 strings.
2. Bass guitars: 4 × 4 = 16 strings.
3. Total: 54 + 16 = 70 strings.
1407941946.stepsTl:
1. Guitars: 9 × 6 = 54 strings.
2. Bass guitars: 4 × 4 = 16 strings.
3. Total: 54 + 16 = 70 strings.
1407941946.hint: Work out each type of guitar separately, then add.
1407941946.hintTl: I-compute muna ang bawat klase ng guitar, tapos i-add.
1407941946.whyB: 54 counts only the six-string guitars and forgets the basses.

1511106379.text: A parking area has 15 cars (4 wheels each) and 8 tricycles (3 wheels each). How many wheels are there in all?
1511106379.steps:
1. Cars: 15 × 4 = 60 wheels.
2. Tricycles: 8 × 3 = 24 wheels.
3. Total: 60 + 24 = 84 wheels.
1511106379.stepsTl:
1. Cars: 15 × 4 = 60 wheels.
2. Tricycles: 8 × 3 = 24 wheels.
3. Total: 60 + 24 = 84 wheels.
1511106379.hint: Count the wheels for each kind of vehicle separately, then add.
1511106379.hintTl: Bilangin muna ang gulong ng bawat klase ng sasakyan, tapos i-add.
1511106379.whyC: 92 gives each tricycle 4 wheels like a car.

161148794.explanation: Each machine makes 1 product in 2 hours. 4 machines working at the same time make 4 products in the same 2 hours.
161148794.explanationTl: Bawat machine ay gumagawa ng 1 product sa 2 hours. Kaya ang 4 machines ay gagawa ng 4 products sa 2 hours din.
161148794.steps:
1. 2 machines make 2 products in 2 hours, so 1 machine makes 1 product in 2 hours.
2. 4 machines each make 1 product at the same time.
3. Time = 2 hours.
161148794.stepsTl:
1. 2 machines, 2 products, 2 hours: kaya 1 machine = 1 product sa 2 hours.
2. Sabay-sabay gumagawa ang 4 machines, tig-iisang product.
3. Time = 2 hours.
161148794.hintTl: Alamin muna ang kaya ng ISANG tao kada oras o araw.
161148794.whyB: 4 hours doubles the time because the products doubled, but the machines doubled too.
161148794.whyC: 1 hour halves the time because the machines doubled, but the products doubled too.
161148794.whyD: 3 hours has no basis; each machine still takes 2 hours per product.

436461011.explanation: Each teacher grades 1 paper in 6 hours. 12 teachers grade 12 papers at the same time, so it still takes 6 hours.
436461011.explanationTl: Bawat teacher ay naka-grade ng 1 paper sa 6 hours. Sabay-sabay ang 12 teachers, kaya 6 hours pa rin.
436461011.steps:
1. 6 teachers grade 6 papers in 6 hours, so 1 teacher grades 1 paper in 6 hours.
2. 12 teachers each grade 1 paper at the same time.
3. Time = 6 hours.
436461011.stepsTl:
1. 6 teachers, 6 papers, 6 hours: kaya 1 teacher = 1 paper sa 6 hours.
2. Sabay-sabay ang 12 teachers, tig-iisang paper.
3. Time = 6 hours.
436461011.hintTl: Alamin muna ang kaya ng ISANG tao kada oras o araw.
436461011.whyB: 12 hours doubles the time for double the papers, but the teachers doubled too.
436461011.whyC: 3 hours halves the time for double the teachers, but the papers doubled too.
436461011.whyD: 9 hours has no basis; each teacher still takes 6 hours per paper.

1495293733.text: If 6 workers build 6 walls in 6 days, how many days will 3 workers take to build 6 walls?
1495293733.explanation: Each worker builds 1 wall in 6 days. 3 workers build 3 walls every 6 days, so 6 walls take 2 × 6 = 12 days.
1495293733.explanationTl: Bawat worker ay 1 wall sa 6 days. Ang 3 workers ay 3 walls kada 6 days, kaya ang 6 walls ay 12 days.
1495293733.steps:
1. 1 worker builds 1 wall in 6 days.
2. 3 workers build 3 walls in 6 days.
3. 6 walls is twice as many: 2 × 6 = 12 days.
1495293733.stepsTl:
1. 1 worker = 1 wall sa 6 days.
2. 3 workers = 3 walls sa 6 days.
3. Doble ang walls (6), kaya 2 × 6 = 12 days.
1495293733.hintTl: Alamin muna ang kaya ng ISANG tao kada oras o araw.
1495293733.whyA: 6 days is the time for 3 workers to build 3 walls; here they must build 6.
1495293733.whyB: 3 days halves the time, but fewer workers means MORE time, not less.
1495293733.whyD: 9 days adds only half again; with half the workers and the same walls, the time doubles.

2043291122.text: If 4 mechanics fix 4 cars in 4 hours, how many hours will 2 mechanics take to fix 4 cars?
2043291122.explanation: Each mechanic fixes 1 car in 4 hours. 2 mechanics fix 2 cars every 4 hours, so 4 cars take 2 × 4 = 8 hours.
2043291122.explanationTl: Bawat mechanic ay 1 car sa 4 hours. Ang 2 mechanics ay 2 cars kada 4 hours, kaya ang 4 cars ay 8 hours.
2043291122.steps:
1. 1 mechanic fixes 1 car in 4 hours.
2. 2 mechanics fix 2 cars in 4 hours.
3. 4 cars is twice as many: 2 × 4 = 8 hours.
2043291122.stepsTl:
1. 1 mechanic = 1 car sa 4 hours.
2. 2 mechanics = 2 cars sa 4 hours.
3. Doble ang cars (4), kaya 2 × 4 = 8 hours.
2043291122.hintTl: Alamin muna ang kaya ng ISANG tao kada oras o araw.
2043291122.whyA: 4 hours is the time for 4 mechanics; with half the mechanics it takes longer.
2043291122.whyB: 2 hours halves the time, but fewer mechanics means MORE time, not less.
2043291122.whyD: 6 hours adds only half again; with half the mechanics and the same cars, the time doubles.

1136378611.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites in temperature; in the same way, light and dark are opposites in brightness.
1136378611.hint: Ask what relationship hot and cold have, then find the word with that same relationship to light.
1136378611.whyB: Bright is close in meaning to light, not its opposite; the pair needs opposites.
1136378611.whyC: A lamp gives off light; that is a source relationship, not opposites like hot and cold.
1136378611.whyD: Day is when there is light; it is associated with light, not its opposite.
1136378611.explanationTl: Magkasalungat ang hot at cold. Kaya ang kapareho niyan para sa light ay ang kabaligtaran niya, which is dark.
1136378611.hintTl: Tingnan mo muna kung ano ang relationship ng hot at cold, tapos hanapin mo 'yung ganun din sa light.

2128945234.hint: Lucid is often used for writing or thinking that is easy to follow. Look for the opposite.
2128945234.whyA: Clear is a synonym of lucid, not an antonym.
2128945234.whyC: Understandable means the same as lucid; the question asks for the opposite.
2128945234.whyD: Coherent (logical and easy to follow) is close to lucid, not its opposite.
2128945234.explanationTl: Ang lucid ay malinaw at madaling intindihin. Kaya ang antonym niya ay confusing, 'yung nakakalito.
2128945234.hintTl: Ginagamit ang lucid para sa paliwanag na madaling sundan. Hanapin mo 'yung kabaligtaran.

209984142.text: Which word in the phrase 'a herd of cattles' is incorrect?
209984142.explanation: 'Cattle' is already a plural noun and never takes -s, so the correct phrase is 'a herd of cattle'.
209984142.hint: One of these nouns has the same form whether you mean one group or many animals.
209984142.whyA: The article 'a' correctly goes with the singular noun 'herd'.
209984142.whyB: 'Herd' is the right collective noun for cattle.
209984142.whyC: 'Of' is the correct preposition after a collective noun ('a herd of', 'a flock of').
209984142.explanationTl: Plural na talaga ang 'cattle', kaya hindi na nilalagyan ng -s. Ang tama ay 'a herd of cattle'.
209984142.hintTl: May isang noun dito na plural na kahit walang -s.

238952314.hint: Check whether every item in the list has the same grammatical form.
238952314.whyA: Mixes infinitives (to swim, to hike) with a gerund (running).
238952314.whyC: Mixes base verbs (swim, run) with a gerund (hiking), and 'likes swim' is ungrammatical.
238952314.whyD: Starts with infinitives (to swim, run) but ends with a gerund (hiking).
238952314.explanationTl: Sa parallelism, dapat pare-pareho ang form ng mga nasa listahan. Sa B, lahat -ing (gerund): swimming, running, hiking.
238952314.hintTl: Tingnan mo kung pare-pareho ang anyo ng bawat item sa listahan.

542674840.explanation: Intricate means very complex and full of detail, which is why readers could not predict the ending.
542674840.hint: The clue is 'couldn't predict the ending'. What kind of plot is hard to predict?
542674840.whyB: A simple plot is easy to predict, the opposite of what the sentence describes.
542674840.whyC: A boring plot is dull, but dullness does not make an ending unpredictable.
542674840.whyD: A familiar plot follows patterns readers know, so it is easier to predict.
542674840.explanationTl: Ang intricate ay sobrang complex at maraming detalye, kaya hindi mahulaan ng readers ang ending.
542674840.hintTl: Ang clue ay 'couldn't predict the ending'. Anong klaseng plot ang mahirap hulaan?

628174097.explanation: 'Inadvertent' means not done on purpose, so an inadvertent error is an unintentional one.
628174097.hint: The prefix 'in-' often means 'not'. 'Advertent' relates to paying attention.
628174097.whyA: Intentional is the opposite of inadvertent.
628174097.whyC: Deliberate means done on purpose, the opposite of inadvertent.
628174097.whyD: Planned means arranged in advance, the opposite of an accidental error.
628174097.explanationTl: Ang inadvertent ay hindi sinasadya. Kaya ang inadvertent error ay unintentional, aksidente lang.
628174097.hintTl: Ang prefix na 'in-' ay madalas 'not' ang ibig sabihin.

1307000080.text: The flock of birds _____ making its way south.
1307000080.explanation: The subject is 'flock', a collective noun acting as one unit (the sentence says 'its way'), so it takes the singular verb 'is'. 'Of birds' does not change the subject.
1307000080.hint: Find the real subject. Is it 'flock' or 'birds'? The word 'its' is a clue.
1307000080.whyB: 'Are' agrees with 'birds', but 'birds' is inside the 'of' phrase; the subject is 'flock'.
1307000080.whyC: 'Were' is plural; the singular subject 'flock' (and 'its') needs a singular verb.
1307000080.whyD: 'Have making' is ungrammatical; the -ing form needs a form of 'be'.
1307000080.explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'flock', hindi 'birds'. Isang grupo siya na kumikilos as one unit (kaya 'its'), so singular ang verb: 'is'.
1307000080.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang totoong subject. 'Flock' ba o 'birds'? Clue ang salitang 'its'.

1980431187.text: The number of books on the shelf _____ ten.
1980431187.explanation: 'The number of' refers to a single total, so it takes a singular verb: 'The number of books is ten.' (Compare: 'A number of books are missing.')
1980431187.hint: Is the subject the books themselves, or one total count?
1980431187.whyB: 'Are' agrees with 'books', but the subject is 'the number', which is singular.
1980431187.whyD: 'Have ten' does not state the count; the sentence needs a linking verb, 'is'.
1980431187.explanationTl: Ang 'the number of' ay isang total lang, kaya singular: 'is'. Iba 'yan sa 'a number of', na plural ('are').
1980431187.hintTl: Ang subject ba ay 'yung mga libro, o 'yung isang bilang (total)?

272174356.text: What does the sentence 'She studied hard, yet she failed.' imply?
272174356.optionB: She failed even though she made an effort.
272174356.optionC: She did not study for the exam.
272174356.optionD: She failed because she studied too hard.
272174356.explanation: 'Yet' signals contrast: the failure happened in spite of her hard studying.
272174356.hint: Focus on the word 'yet'. What kind of relationship does it show?
272174356.whyA: The sentence shows the opposite: hard study did not guarantee her success.
272174356.whyC: The sentence states plainly that she studied hard.
272174356.whyD: 'Yet' shows contrast, not cause; nothing says studying caused the failure.
272174356.explanationTl: Ang 'yet' ay nagpapakita ng contrast. Ibig sabihin, bumagsak siya kahit nag-aral siya nang mabuti.
272174356.hintTl: Tutukan mo ang salitang 'yet'. Anong klaseng relationship ang pinapakita niya?

386851684.explanation: The correct spelling is 'calendar', ending in -ar. 'Calender' is a common misspelling.
386851684.hint: Think about the ending of the word for the chart of days and months: -er or -ar?
386851684.explanationTl: Ang tamang spelling ay 'calendar', -ar ang dulo. Madalas mali ang 'calender'.
386851684.hintTl: Tingnan mo ang dulo ng salita: -er ba o -ar?

1602142674.hint: Remember the rule about i and e after the letter c.
1602142674.whyA: Swaps the vowels: after c it is 'ei', not 'ie'.
1602142674.explanationTl: Tama ang 'receive'. Sundin ang rule na 'i before e, except after c', kaya 'cei' ang tama.
1602142674.hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang rule tungkol sa i at e pagkatapos ng letter c.

162904311.hint: An eccentric person does things differently from most people.
162904311.whyA: Normal is close to the opposite of eccentric.
162904311.whyC: Conventional means following usual customs, the opposite of eccentric.
162904311.whyD: Standard means usual or ordinary, the opposite of eccentric.
162904311.explanationTl: Ang eccentric ay kakaiba o hindi pangkaraniwan ang kilos, kaya unconventional ang pinakamalapit.
162904311.hintTl: Ang taong eccentric ay iba ang gawi kumpara sa karamihan.

375555613.explanation: Tenacious means holding on firmly and not giving up easily, so its synonym is persistent.
375555613.hint: A tenacious person keeps going even when things get hard.
375555613.whyA: Weak suggests lack of strength, nearly the opposite of tenacious.
375555613.whyC: Hesitant means unsure and slow to act, not determined.
375555613.whyD: Feeble means weak, the opposite of the firm grip implied by tenacious.
375555613.explanationTl: Ang tenacious ay matiyaga at hindi basta sumusuko, kaya ang synonym niya ay persistent.
375555613.hintTl: Ang taong tenacious ay tuloy lang kahit mahirap na.

706599274.hint: A stringent policy leaves very little room for exceptions.
706599274.whyA: Lenient means easygoing, the opposite of stringent.
706599274.whyC: Flexible means open to change, the opposite of stringent.
706599274.whyD: Loose means not strict, the opposite of stringent.
706599274.explanationTl: Ang stringent ay mahigpit, kaya ang stringent na policy ay strict, walang palusot.
