1130976751.hintTl: Dumadaan ito sa valley region sa northeastern Luzon.

1232696367.text: Which city is the capital of the Philippines?
1232696367.explanation: Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976) restored Manila as the capital of the Philippines; Quezon City had held that status since 1948 under RA 333.
1232696367.hint: It is the city where Malacañang Palace stands.
1232696367.whyA: Quezon City was the capital from 1948 to 1976, but PD 940 restored Manila.
1232696367.whyC: Makati is the main business district, not the capital.
1232696367.whyD: Pasay hosts government offices such as the Senate but is not the capital.
1232696367.explanationTl: Sa Presidential Decree No. 940 (1976), ibinalik ang Manila bilang capital ng Pilipinas; dati, Quezon City ang capital mula 1948 under RA 333.

1355532793.text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), once common in refrigerators and air conditioners, are being phased out mainly because they:
1355532793.explanation: CFCs release chlorine in the upper atmosphere, which breaks down ozone. The Montreal Protocol, which the Philippines has joined, phases them out.
1355532793.hint: Think of the layer of the atmosphere that shields us from ultraviolet rays.
1355532793.whyB: Acid rain comes mainly from sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, not CFCs.
1355532793.whyD: CFCs are gases that rise into the atmosphere; groundwater contamination is not their main harm.
1355532793.explanationTl: Ang CFCs ay naglalabas ng chlorine sa upper atmosphere, at sinisira nito ang ozone. Kaya pine-phase out sila sa ilalim ng Montreal Protocol, na sinalihan din ng Pilipinas.
1355532793.hintTl: Isipin mo yung layer ng atmosphere na nagpo-protect sa atin sa UV rays.

1516273769.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869, arranging elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps for elements not yet discovered.
1516273769.hint: He was a Russian chemist who predicted elements that had not yet been found.
1516273769.whyB: Marie Curie discovered polonium and radium; she did not create the periodic table.
1516273769.whyC: John Dalton proposed the modern atomic theory.
1516273769.whyD: Antoine Lavoisier is called the father of modern chemistry for his work on combustion and conservation of mass.
1516273769.explanationTl: Si Dmitri Mendeleev ang nag-publish ng periodic table noong 1869; inayos niya ang elements by atomic mass at nag-iwan ng gaps para sa elements na hindi pa natutuklasan.
1516273769.hintTl: Russian chemist siya na naka-predict ng elements na hindi pa nadi-discover noon.

1595912791.text: Who formulated the law of universal gravitation?
1595912791.explanation: Isaac Newton stated the law of universal gravitation in his Principia (1687): every mass attracts every other mass.
1595912791.hint: He was an English scientist who also gave us three laws of motion.
1595912791.whyA: Einstein later explained gravity as curved spacetime (general relativity, 1915), but the law of universal gravitation is Newton’s.
1595912791.whyC: Galileo studied falling bodies before Newton but did not formulate universal gravitation.
1595912791.whyD: Stephen Hawking studied black holes and cosmology in the 20th century.
1595912791.explanationTl: Si Isaac Newton ang nag-formulate ng law of universal gravitation sa Principia (1687): lahat ng may mass ay nag-a-attract sa isa’t isa.
1595912791.hintTl: English scientist siya na may three laws of motion din.

1774245905.text: The Banaue Rice Terraces are found in which province?
1774245905.explanation: The Banaue Rice Terraces are in Banaue, Ifugao, in the Cordillera Administrative Region, carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people.
1774245905.hint: The province shares its name with the people who built the terraces.
1774245905.whyA: Benguet is known for Baguio and highland vegetables, not the Banaue terraces.
1774245905.whyB: Mountain Province is a neighboring Cordillera province (home of Sagada), but Banaue is not there.
1774245905.whyC: Kalinga is another Cordillera province, north of Ifugao.
1774245905.explanationTl: Ang Banaue Rice Terraces ay nasa Banaue, Ifugao, sa Cordillera Administrative Region; ginawa ito ng mga Ifugao sa bundok.
1774245905.hintTl: Kapangalan ng province ang mga taong gumawa ng terraces.

1923130828.text: Who wrote the Tagalog metrical romance "Florante at Laura"?
1923130828.explanation: "Florante at Laura" (1838) is the awit written by Francisco Balagtas (Francisco Baltazar), a classic of Tagalog poetry.
1923130828.hint: The Philippine debate in verse, the balagtasan, is named after him.
1923130828.whyA: Jose Rizal wrote the novels "Noli Me Tangere" and "El Filibusterismo."
1923130828.whyB: Severino Reyes is known for the zarzuela "Walang Sugat" and the Lola Basyang stories.
1923130828.whyD: Jose Corazon de Jesus was the first "Hari ng Balagtasan," a 20th-century poet.
1923130828.explanationTl: Ang "Florante at Laura" (1838) ay isinulat ni Francisco Balagtas (Francisco Baltazar); classic ito ng Tagalog poetry.

1929580637.explanation: Carbon’s chemical symbol is the single letter C.
1929580637.hint: Carbon’s symbol is just one letter.
1929580637.explanationTl: Ang chemical symbol ng carbon ay C, isang letter lang.
1929580637.hintTl: Isang letter lang ang symbol ng carbon.

2043994268.text: What is the longest mountain range in the Philippines?
2043994268.explanation: The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, running along the eastern side of Luzon from Cagayan down to Quezon province.
2043994268.hint: It runs along Luzon’s Pacific coast and helps shield the island from typhoons.
2043994268.whyA: The Cordillera Central is the highest range in northern Luzon but shorter than the Sierra Madre.
2043994268.whyB: The Caraballo Mountains are a short range linking the Cordillera and the Sierra Madre.
2043994268.whyC: The Zambales Mountains run along western Luzon and are much shorter.
2043994268.explanationTl: Ang Sierra Madre ang pinakamahabang mountain range sa Pilipinas; dumadaan ito sa eastern side ng Luzon mula Cagayan hanggang Quezon.
2043994268.hintTl: Nasa Pacific side ito ng Luzon at nakakatulong mag-shield laban sa bagyo.

1788748540.text: Which law is known as the Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines?
1788748540.explanation: Republic Act No. 8491 (1998), the Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines, prescribes the national flag, anthem, motto, coat of arms and other heraldic items.
1788748540.hint: This 1998 law covers the flag, the anthem and the coat of arms.
1788748540.whyB: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.
1788748540.whyC: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
1788748540.whyD: RA 7160 is the Local Government Code of 1991.
1788748540.explanationTl: Ang Republic Act No. 8491 (1998) ang Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines. Dito nakasaad ang rules sa national flag, anthem, motto, coat of arms at iba pang heraldic items.
1788748540.hintTl: Batas ito noong 1998 tungkol sa flag, anthem at coat of arms.

340685609.steps:

340685609.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang u = 20 at v = 4: t = 20 ÷ 4.
2. I-divide: t = 5.

466653163.explanationTl: Para makuha ang x, i-divide ang 81 sa 9: x = 9.

798361226.explanationTl: Para makuha ang x, i-divide ang 25 sa 5: x = 5.

1411236690.explanationTl: Para makuha ang x, i-divide ang 49 sa 7: x = 7.

1528286468.steps:
1. Substitute n = 10 and p = 4: m = 10 − 4.
2. Subtract: m = 6.
1528286468.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang n = 10 at p = 4: m = 10 − 4.
2. I-subtract: m = 6.
1528286468.whyC: 5 is a subtraction slip: 10 − 4 is 6, not 5.
1528286468.whyD: 7 is a subtraction slip: 10 − 4 is 6, not 7.

1622931909.steps:
1. Substitute p = 5 and q = 6: o = 5 + 6.
2. Add: o = 11.
1622931909.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang p = 5 at q = 6: o = 5 + 6.

1622931909.whyB: 10 is an addition slip: 5 + 6 is 11, not 10.
1622931909.whyC: 12 is an addition slip: 5 + 6 is 11, not 12.

1844558306.text: If u = v × w and v = 4, w = 5, what is u?
1844558306.steps:
1. Substitute v = 4 and w = 5: u = 4 × 5.
2. Multiply: u = 20.
1844558306.stepsTl:
1. Ipalit ang v = 4 at w = 5: u = 4 × 5.
2. I-multiply: u = 20.
1844558306.whyD: 25 is 5 × 5: it uses w twice instead of v × w.

907670181.steps:
1. Simplify 4/6 to 2/3 (divide top and bottom by 2).
2. Now the denominators match: 2/3 + 1/3 = 3/3.
3. 3/3 = 1.
907670181.stepsTl:
1. I-simplify ang 4/6 → 2/3 (hatiin sa 2 ang taas at baba).
2. Pareho na ang denominator: 2/3 + 1/3 = 3/3.
3. Ang 3/3 ay 1.
907670181.whyB: 2/3 is just 4/6 simplified; the 1/3 was never added.

1324726266.steps:
1. The denominators are already the same (7).
2. Subtract the numerators: 5 − 2 = 3.
3. Answer: 3/7.
1324726266.stepsTl:
1. Pareho na ang denominator (7).
2. I-subtract ang numerators: 5 − 2 = 3.
3. Sagot: 3/7.
1324726266.whyB: 7/7 adds the numerators (5 + 2) instead of subtracting.
1324726266.whyC: 1/7 is a subtraction slip: 5 − 2 is 3, not 1.
1324726266.whyD: 4/7 is a subtraction slip: 5 − 2 is 3, not 4.
1324726266.explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya i-subtract lang ang numerators: 5 − 2 = 3, so 3/7.

1501371987.steps:
1. The denominators are the same (3).
2. Add only the numerators: 1 + 1 = 2.
3. Keep the denominator: 2/3.
1501371987.stepsTl:
1. Pareho ang denominator (3).
2. Numerators lang ang i-add: 1 + 1 = 2.
3. Panatilihin ang denominator: 2/3.
1501371987.whyB: 2/6 adds the denominators too (3 + 3); only the numerators are added.
1501371987.whyC: 1/9 multiplies the fractions instead of adding them.
1501371987.whyD: 1/6 adds the denominators but keeps one numerator.
1501371987.explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya numerators lang ang i-add: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3.

118872779.text: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
118872779.explanation: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon that is 6 × 180° = 1,080°, and a regular octagon has 8 equal angles, so each is 1,080° ÷ 8 = 135°.
118872779.steps:
1. An octagon has 8 sides, so n = 8.
2. Sum of interior angles: (8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°.
3. Each angle: 1,080° ÷ 8 = 135°.
118872779.stepsTl:
1. Ang octagon ay may 8 sides, so n = 8.
2. Sum ng interior angles: (8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°.
3. Bawat angle: 1,080° ÷ 8 = 135°.
118872779.hint: Find the total of all interior angles first, then share it equally among the angles.
118872779.hintTl: Hanapin muna ang total ng lahat ng interior angles, tapos hatiin nang pantay.
118872779.whyA: 120° is each angle of a regular hexagon (6 sides), not an octagon.
118872779.whyC: 144° is each angle of a regular decagon (10 sides).
118872779.whyD: 1,080° is the SUM of all eight angles, not one angle.
118872779.explanationTl: Sum ng interior angles ng octagon = (8 − 2) × 180° = 1,080°. Hatiin sa 8 kasi pantay-pantay: 135° bawat isa.

490956332.text: A microwave oven priced at ₱3,000 is sold at a 33% discount. What is the final price?
490956332.whyD: ₱1,900 takes off ₱1,100, which is more than 33% of ₱3,000 (₱990).

1602985521.explanationTl: Ang 9% ng 100 ay 9 lang, kasi ang percent ay "sa bawat 100".

1620882769.text: A wallet priced at ₱500 is marked 20% off, and the cashier then takes another 10% off the sale price. What is the final price?
1620882769.explanation: After 20% off, the price is 0.8 × ₱500 = ₱400. The extra 10% is taken from ₱400, so the final price is 0.9 × ₱400 = ₱360.
1620882769.steps:
1. First discount: 0.8 × ₱500 = ₱400.
2. Second discount is on ₱400: 0.9 × ₱400 = ₱360.
3. Final price: ₱360.
1620882769.stepsTl:
1. Unang discount: 0.8 × ₱500 = ₱400.
2. Ang pangalawang 10% ay sa ₱400 na: 0.9 × ₱400 = ₱360.
3. Final price: ₱360.
1620882769.hint: The second discount is taken from the already-reduced price, not from the original.
1620882769.hintTl: Ang pangalawang discount ay sa bagong presyo kinukuha, hindi sa original.
1620882769.whyA: ₱350 adds the discounts into one 30% discount; the second 10% applies to ₱400, not ₱500.
1620882769.explanationTl: Una, 20% off: ₱500 → ₱400. Tapos 10% off sa ₱400 (₱40): ₱360. Hindi ito pareho ng 30% off.

2072066813.text: A pair of shoes is priced at ₱1,250. It is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
2072066813.explanation: The discount is 20% of ₱1,250 = ₱250, so the sale price is ₱1,250 − ₱250 = ₱1,000.
2072066813.hint: Find the discount amount first, then subtract it from the original price.
2072066813.whyB: ₱250 is the discount amount, not the price after the discount.
2072066813.explanationTl: Ang discount ay 20% ng ₱1,250 = ₱250, kaya ang sale price ay ₱1,250 − ₱250 = ₱1,000.
2072066813.hintTl: Hanapin muna ang discount amount, tapos ibawas sa original price.

2083639282.whyC: 35 is more than 20%: 10% of 150 is 15, so 20% is 30.
2083639282.whyD: 40 is more than 20%: 10% of 150 is 15, so 20% is 30.

548274261.steps:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 60 km ÷ 3 h = 20 km/h.
548274261.stepsTl:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 60 km ÷ 3 h = 20 km/h.
548274261.whyB: 15 km/h would cover only 45 km in 3 hours.
548274261.whyC: 25 km/h would cover 75 km in 3 hours.
548274261.whyD: 30 km/h would cover 90 km in 3 hours.

1275863076.steps:
1. Change minutes to hours: 50 min = 50/60 = 5/6 h.
2. Speed = 10 km ÷ 5/6 h = 10 × 6/5 = 12 km/h.
1275863076.stepsTl:
1. Gawing hours ang minutes: 50 min = 5/6 h.
2. Speed = 10 ÷ 5/6 = 10 × 6/5 = 12 km/h.
1275863076.whyB: 10 km/h would take a full 60 minutes for 10 km.
1275863076.whyC: 15 km/h would take 40 minutes for 10 km.
1275863076.whyD: 20 km/h would take 30 minutes for 10 km.
1275863076.explanationTl: Ang 50 minutes ay 5/6 ng isang oras. 10 ÷ 5/6 = 12 km/h.

1740064796.steps:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 180 km ÷ 3 h = 60 km/h.
1740064796.stepsTl:
1. Speed = distance ÷ time.
2. 180 km ÷ 3 h = 60 km/h.
1740064796.whyB: 50 km/h would cover only 150 km in 3 hours.
1740064796.whyC: 70 km/h would cover 210 km in 3 hours.
1740064796.whyD: 80 km/h would cover 240 km in 3 hours.

1941691772.text: A bus leaves Butuan at 8:30 AM and reaches a town 225 km away at 12:15 PM. What is its average speed?
1941691772.explanation: From 8:30 AM to 12:15 PM is 3 hours 45 minutes = 3.75 h. Average speed = 225 km ÷ 3.75 h = 60 km/h.
1941691772.steps:
1. Travel time: 8:30 AM to 12:15 PM = 3 h 45 min.
2. 45 min = 0.75 h, so time = 3.75 h.
3. Speed = 225 km ÷ 3.75 h = 60 km/h.
1941691772.stepsTl:
1. Oras ng biyahe: 8:30 AM hanggang 12:15 PM = 3 h 45 min.
2. Ang 45 min ay 0.75 h, kaya 3.75 h.
3. Speed = 225 ÷ 3.75 = 60 km/h.
1941691772.hint: Work out the travel time in hours first, including the minutes.
1941691772.hintTl: Kunin muna ang tagal ng biyahe in hours, kasama ang minutes.
1941691772.whyB: 75 km/h uses 3 hours and drops the 45 minutes.
1941691772.whyC: 50 km/h uses 4.5 hours, reading 45 minutes as 1.5 hours.
1941691772.whyD: 56.25 km/h rounds the trip up to 4 hours.
1941691772.explanationTl: Ang biyahe ay 3 hours 45 minutes = 3.75 h. 225 ÷ 3.75 = 60 km/h.

108426720.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 320, 160, 80, 40, ?
108426720.explanation: Each term is half of the one before it, so the next term is 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
108426720.hint: Compare each term with the one before it: what is it divided by?
108426720.whyC: 0 subtracts 40 again, treating the series as a fixed subtraction.
108426720.whyD: 80 doubles instead of halving, reversing the direction of the series.
108426720.explanationTl: Hinahati sa dalawa ang bawat term, kaya ang susunod ay 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
108426720.hintTl: Ikumpara ang bawat term sa nauna: ilan ang ipinang-divide?
108426720.stepsTl:
1. Bawat term ay kalahati ng nauna (160 ÷ 320 = 1/2, 80 ÷ 160 = 1/2, 40 ÷ 80 = 1/2).
2. Ang rule ay ÷2.
3. 40 ÷ 2 = 20.

381284277.whyB: 30 subtracts only 10; every step drops by 20.
381284277.whyD: 0 skips a term: it is the term after 20.

891441518.whyB: 81 is 9², but the bases are even: 2, 4, 6, 8, then 10.
891441518.whyC: 121 is 11²; the next even base after 8 is 10, not 11.
891441518.explanationTl: Squares ng even numbers: 2², 4², 6², 8², kaya susunod ang 10² = 100.

899803267.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 4, 12, 36, 108, ?
899803267.explanation: Each term is three times the one before it, so the next term is 108 × 3 = 324.
899803267.hint: Compare each term with the one before it: is it added to, or multiplied?
899803267.whyC: 144 adds 36, treating the series as adding a fixed amount.
899803267.explanationTl: Tini-triple ang bawat term, kaya ang susunod ay 108 × 3 = 324.
899803267.hintTl: Ikumpara ang bawat term sa nauna: dinadagdagan ba o mini-multiply?

950767701.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
950767701.whyD: 7 goes down; the series is increasing by 2.

1401195273.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
1401195273.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, so the next difference is 13: 35 + 13 = 48. Each term is also n² − 1 (2² − 1 = 3 up to 7² − 1 = 48).
1401195273.steps:
1. Differences: 8 − 3 = 5, 15 − 8 = 7, 24 − 15 = 9, 35 − 24 = 11.
2. The differences go up by 2, so the next difference is 13.
3. 35 + 13 = 48.
4. Check: the terms are 2² − 1, 3² − 1, ..., 6² − 1, so next is 7² − 1 = 48.
1401195273.hint: Look at how much each term grows, then how the growth itself changes.
1401195273.whyB: 46 adds 11 again, as if the differences stayed constant.
1401195273.whyD: 50 adds 15, skipping a step in the odd-number differences.
1401195273.explanationTl: Ang differences ay 5, 7, 9, 11, kaya ang next difference ay 13: 35 + 13 = 48. Pwede rin tingnan as n² − 1 (7² − 1 = 48).
1401195273.hintTl: Tingnan mo kung magkano ang dagdag sa bawat term, tapos kung paano nagbabago ang dagdag.
1401195273.stepsTl:
1. Differences: 5, 7, 9, 11.
2. Tumataas ng 2 ang differences, kaya 13 ang susunod.
3. 35 + 13 = 48.
4. Check: 7² − 1 = 48.

1529363246.text: What is the next number in the sequence: 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, ?
1529363246.explanation: Each term is 6 more than the one before it, so the next term is 31 + 6 = 37.
1529363246.hint: Subtract each term from the next one and see if the gap stays the same.
1529363246.whyD: 43 adds 12, skipping one term of the series.
1529363246.explanationTl: Plus 6 ang bawat term, kaya ang susunod ay 31 + 6 = 37.
1529363246.hintTl: Ibawas ang bawat term sa kasunod nito at tingnan kung pareho ang pagitan.

812756266.whyC: 25 is the average of 20 and 30 only.
812756266.whyD: 30 is the largest number, not the average.
812756266.explanationTl: I-add lahat (60) tapos hatiin sa 3: average = 20.

894776864.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 2 appears twice; 1, 3 and 4 appear once, so the mode is 2.
894776864.steps:
1. Count each value: 1 once, 2 twice, 3 once, 4 once.
2. The most frequent value is 2.
894776864.stepsTl:
1. Bilangin: 1 isang beses, 2 dalawang beses, 3 isa, 4 isa.
2. Pinakamadalas: 2.
894776864.hint: Mode = the value that appears most often.
894776864.hintTl: Mode = ang value na pinakamadalas lumabas.
894776864.whyB: 1 appears only once; it is the smallest value, not the most frequent.
894776864.whyD: 4 appears once; it is the largest value, not the most frequent.
894776864.explanationTl: Ang mode ay ang pinakamadalas lumabas. Dalawang beses ang 2, kaya mode = 2.

362914008.text: A square lot has a perimeter of 48 m. What is its area?
362914008.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides, so each side is 48 ÷ 4 = 12 m. Area = 12 × 12 = 144 m².
362914008.steps:
1. Side = perimeter ÷ 4 = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 m.
2. Area = side × side = 12 × 12 = 144 m².
362914008.hint: Get the length of one side from the perimeter first.
362914008.hintTl: Kunin muna ang haba ng isang side mula sa perimeter.
362914008.whyA: 576 m² uses a side of 24 m (48 ÷ 2), but a square has 4 sides, not 2.
362914008.whyB: 96 m² is 48 × 2, which is not an area formula.
362914008.whyD: 192 m² is 48 × 4: it multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.
362914008.explanationTl: Hatiin sa 4 ang perimeter para sa side: 12 m. Area = 12 × 12 = 144 m².

1770394816.text: Ana bought 7 notebooks at ₱35 each and paid with a ₱500 bill. How much change did she get?
1770394816.explanation: The notebooks cost 7 × ₱35 = ₱245, so her change is ₱500 − ₱245 = ₱255.
1770394816.hint: Find the total cost first, then subtract it from the amount paid.
1770394816.hintTl: Kunin muna ang total na gastos, tapos ibawas sa ibinayad.
1770394816.whyA: ₱245 is the total cost, not the change.
1770394816.whyC: ₱465 subtracts the price of only one notebook.

22064127.text: If 10 workers can build a house in 20 days, how many days will 20 workers take, working at the same rate?
22064127.explanation: The job needs 10 × 20 = 200 worker-days. With 20 workers it takes 200 ÷ 20 = 10 days.
22064127.steps:
1. Total work: 10 workers × 20 days = 200 worker-days.
2. With 20 workers: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 days.
22064127.stepsTl:
1. Total na trabaho: 10 × 20 = 200 worker-days.
2. Kung 20 workers: 200 ÷ 20 = 10 days.
22064127.hint: More workers means fewer days: find the total worker-days first.
22064127.hintTl: Mas maraming tao, mas kaunting araw. Kunin muna ang total worker-days.
22064127.whyC: 5 days halves the time twice; doubling the workers halves it once.
22064127.whyD: 15 days subtracts 5 days instead of halving.
22064127.explanationTl: 200 worker-days ang trabaho (10 × 20). Kung 20 ang workers, 200 ÷ 20 = 10 days.

104286941.explanation: Each writer makes 1 book in 5 months. With 10 writers working at once, 10 books are also done in 5 months.
104286941.steps:
1. 5 writers make 5 books in 5 months, so 1 writer makes 1 book in 5 months.
2. 10 writers each make 1 book at the same time.
3. So 10 books take 5 months.
104286941.stepsTl:
1. Ang 1 writer ay gumagawa ng 1 book sa 5 months.
2. Ang 10 writers ay sabay-sabay, tig-1 book bawat isa.
3. Kaya 5 months pa rin.
104286941.hint: Find how long ONE person takes for ONE item first.
104286941.hintTl: Alamin muna kung gaano katagal ang ISANG tao para sa ISANG item.
104286941.explanationTl: Ang isang writer ay 1 book kada 5 months. Kahit 10 na sila, tig-isa lang sila, kaya 5 months pa rin.
104286941.whyB: 10 months doubles the time because the books doubled, ignoring that the writers doubled too.
104286941.whyC: 2.5 months halves the time for double the writers, ignoring that the books doubled too.
104286941.whyD: 7.5 months has no basis: workers and work both doubled, so time is unchanged.

789045348.explanation: Each driver makes 1 car in 7 hours. With 14 drivers working at once, 14 cars are also done in 7 hours.
789045348.steps:
1. 7 drivers make 7 cars in 7 hours, so 1 driver makes 1 car in 7 hours.
2. 14 drivers each make 1 car at the same time.
3. So 14 cars take 7 hours.
789045348.stepsTl:
1. Ang 1 driver ay gumagawa ng 1 car sa 7 hours.
2. Ang 14 drivers ay sabay-sabay, tig-1 car bawat isa.
3. Kaya 7 hours pa rin.
789045348.hint: Find how long ONE person takes for ONE item first.
789045348.hintTl: Alamin muna kung gaano katagal ang ISANG tao para sa ISANG item.
789045348.explanationTl: Ang isang driver ay 1 car kada 7 hours. Kahit 14 na sila, tig-isa lang sila, kaya 7 hours pa rin.
789045348.whyB: 14 hours doubles the time because the cars doubled, ignoring that the drivers doubled too.
789045348.whyC: 3.5 hours halves the time for double the drivers, ignoring that the cars doubled too.
789045348.whyD: 10.5 hours has no basis: drivers and cars both doubled, so time is unchanged.

882286800.text: Six masons can build a wall in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how many days will 4 masons need to build the same wall?
882286800.explanation: The wall takes 6 × 12 = 72 mason-days of work. With 4 masons it takes 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days, since fewer workers need more time.
882286800.steps:
1. Total work = 6 masons × 12 days = 72 mason-days.
2. Days for 4 masons = 72 ÷ 4 = 18.
3. Check: fewer masons, so more days than 12.
882286800.hint: Fewer workers on the same job need more days, not fewer.
882286800.whyB: 8 uses direct proportion (12 × 4 ÷ 6), but fewer workers need more time.
882286800.whyC: 10 subtracts the 2 missing masons from the 12 days.
882286800.whyD: 24 doubles the days, as if half the masons were working.
882286800.explanationTl: Ang wall ay 6 × 12 = 72 mason-days na trabaho. Kung 4 masons lang, 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days, kasi mas kaunti ang tao, mas matagal.
882286800.hintTl: Kapag mas kaunti ang workers sa parehong trabaho, mas maraming araw ang kailangan.
882286800.stepsTl:
1. Total work = 6 masons × 12 days = 72 mason-days.
2. Para sa 4 masons: 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days.
3. Check: mas kaunti ang masons, kaya dapat higit sa 12 days.

1123632898.explanation: Each tailor makes 1 suit in 6 days. With 3 tailors working at once, 3 suits are also done in 6 days.
1123632898.steps:
1. 6 tailors make 6 suits in 6 days, so 1 tailor makes 1 suit in 6 days.
2. 3 tailors each make 1 suit at the same time.
3. So 3 suits take 6 days.
1123632898.stepsTl:
1. Ang 1 tailor ay gumagawa ng 1 suit sa 6 days.
2. Ang 3 tailors ay sabay-sabay, tig-1 suit bawat isa.
3. Kaya 6 days pa rin.
1123632898.hint: Find how long ONE person takes for ONE item first.
1123632898.hintTl: Alamin muna kung gaano katagal ang ISANG tao para sa ISANG item.
1123632898.explanationTl: Ang isang tailor ay 1 suit kada 6 days. Kahit 3 na sila, tig-isa lang sila, kaya 6 days pa rin.
1123632898.whyB: 3 days halves the time because the suits halved, ignoring that the tailors halved too.
1123632898.whyC: 12 days doubles the time for half the tailors, ignoring that the suits halved too.
1123632898.whyD: 9 days has no basis: tailors and suits both halved, so time is unchanged.

575804354.hint: Think of the main way each animal moves.
575804354.whyB: Walking is how land animals move; fish have no legs.
575804354.whyC: Running needs legs; it is not a fish's natural movement.
575804354.whyD: Some fish leap, but jumping is not their main way of moving.
575804354.explanationTl: Ang ibon ay lumilipad (fly), ang isda naman ay lumalangoy (swim). Parehong relationship: animal to its main way of moving.
575804354.hintTl: Isipin mo kung paano talaga gumagalaw ang bawat hayop.

1921384393.hint: What is each place mostly made of?
1921384393.whyB: Heat describes a desert's climate, not what it is made of.
1921384393.whyC: A cactus lives in the desert; it is not what the desert is made of.
1921384393.whyD: A camel lives in the desert; this is a habitat link, not a 'made of' link.
1921384393.explanationTl: Ang ocean ay binubuo ng water, at ang desert ay binubuo ng sand. Ang relationship ay place to what it is made of.
1921384393.hintTl: Ano ang pangunahing laman o bumubuo sa bawat lugar?

313375559.hint: Benevolent describes someone who wishes others well. Find its opposite.
313375559.whyA: Kind is a synonym of benevolent, not an antonym.
313375559.whyC: Generous is close in meaning to benevolent, not opposite.
313375559.whyD: Friendly is similar to benevolent, not its opposite.
313375559.explanationTl: Ang benevolent ay mabait at may mabuting intensyon sa iba, kaya ang opposite ay malicious, ibig sabihin gustong manakit o mamerwisyo.
313375559.hintTl: Ang benevolent ay taong gusto ang mabuti para sa iba. Hanapin ang kabaligtaran.

782317538.optionA: Yesterday, they was going to the market.
782317538.optionB: Yesterday, they were going to the market.
782317538.optionC: Yesterday, they is going to the market.
782317538.optionD: Yesterday, they are going to the market.
782317538.explanation: 'Yesterday' calls for the past tense, and the plural subject 'they' takes 'were', giving the past continuous 'they were going'.
782317538.hint: Check two things: the time word and whether the subject is singular or plural.
782317538.whyA: 'Was' is singular; 'they' is plural and needs 'were'.
782317538.whyC: 'Is' is singular and present; 'they' needs a plural past form.
782317538.whyD: 'Are' agrees with 'they' but is present tense, which clashes with 'yesterday'.
782317538.explanationTl: Dahil may 'yesterday', past tense ang kailangan, at plural ang 'they' kaya 'were' ang tama: 'they were going'.
782317538.hintTl: Tingnan mo ang time word at kung singular o plural ang subject.

1424839539.hint: The speaker is offering a choice between two drinks.
1424839539.whyA: 'So' shows result, not a choice between two things.
1424839539.whyC: 'But' shows contrast, which makes no sense in an offer.
1424839539.whyD: 'And' would offer both drinks together, not a choice of one.
1424839539.explanationTl: Ginagamit ang 'or' kapag pinapapili mo ang tao sa dalawang bagay, kaya 'coffee or tea' ang tama.
1424839539.hintTl: Pinapapili ang tao sa dalawang inumin.

676241558.hint: Article first, then adjectives (quality before color), then the noun.
676241558.whyA: Color adjectives come after quality adjectives, so 'brown quick' is out of order.
676241558.whyC: The article 'the' must come before the adjectives.
676241558.whyD: The article must come first, and 'brown' must follow 'quick'.
676241558.explanationTl: Ang tamang order ay article, tapos adjectives (quality bago color), tapos noun: 'The quick brown fox'.
676241558.hintTl: Article muna, tapos adjectives (quality bago color), saka ang noun.

2064729706.text: Arrange the sentences in logical order: (1) The pan is placed in the oven to bake. (2) The batter is poured into a greased pan. (3) The ingredients are mixed into a smooth batter. (4) The cooled cake is sliced and served.
2064729706.explanation: You must have batter before you can pour it, and it must be in the pan before baking; serving comes last. So the order is mix (3), pour (2), bake (1), serve (4).
2064729706.steps:
1. The batter must exist first: sentence 3 (mix the ingredients).
2. The batter goes into the pan: sentence 2.
3. The pan goes into the oven: sentence 1.
4. The cake is served last: sentence 4.
5. Order: 3-2-1-4.
2064729706.hint: Find the step that every other step depends on.
2064729706.whyB: You cannot pour batter (2) before the ingredients are mixed (3).
2064729706.whyC: Baking (1) cannot come before there is batter in a pan.
2064729706.whyD: The pan cannot be baked (1) before the batter is poured into it (2).
2064729706.explanationTl: Kailangan munang may batter bago ibuhos, at dapat nasa pan na bago i-bake; huli ang pag-serve. Kaya 3-2-1-4.
2064729706.stepsTl:
1. Una, kailangan munang gawin ang batter: sentence 3.
2. Ibuhos ang batter sa pan: sentence 2.
3. Ilagay ang pan sa oven: sentence 1.
4. Huli ang pag-serve: sentence 4.
5. Order: 3-2-1-4.
2064729706.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang step na kailangan muna bago magawa ang iba.

598687627.hint: The base word 'occur' doubles its final consonant before the suffix.
598687627.whyA: Missing the second 'r'; 'occur' doubles the r before '-ence'.
598687627.whyD: Missing the second 'c' and the second 'r'.
598687627.explanationTl: Ang tamang spelling ay 'occurrence': double c, double r, at '-ence' ang dulo.
598687627.hintTl: Sa 'occur', dino-double ang huling consonant bago idagdag ang suffix.

1474941314.explanation: The correct spelling is 'restaurant' (r-e-s-t-a-u-r-a-n-t); the sentence swaps the 'a' and 'u'.
1474941314.hint: Spell each word slowly, letter by letter.
1474941314.explanationTl: Ang tamang spelling ay 'restaurant'; napagpalit ang 'a' at 'u' sa sentence.
1474941314.hintTl: I-spell mo nang dahan-dahan ang bawat word.

163859528.hint: Think of 'lucid' as letting light through, so the point is easy to see.
163859528.whyA: Confusing is the opposite of lucid.
163859528.whyC: Lengthy refers to length, not clarity; a long explanation can still be unclear.
163859528.whyD: Emotional describes feeling, not how clearly something is explained.
163859528.explanationTl: Ang 'lucid' ay malinaw at madaling intindihin, kaya 'clear' ang sagot.
163859528.hintTl: Isipin mo ang 'lucid' na parang may liwanag, kaya madaling makita ang punto.

195027882.explanation: 'Fastidious' means very attentive to accuracy and detail and hard to please; 'meticulous' is the closest meaning.
195027882.hint: A fastidious person notices every small flaw.
195027882.whyA: Lazy means unwilling to work; a fastidious person is careful and exacting.
195027882.whyC: Generous is about giving freely, unrelated to attention to detail.
195027882.whyD: Forgetful means failing to remember; fastidious people tend to miss nothing.
195027882.explanationTl: Ang 'fastidious' ay sobrang maingat at metikuloso sa detalye, kaya 'meticulous' ang sagot.
195027882.hintTl: Ang fastidious na tao ay napapansin kahit maliit na mali.

656936127.hint: A doctor's job is to reduce suffering.
656936127.whyA: Aggravate means to make worse, the opposite of mitigate.
656936127.whyB: Intensify means to make stronger, the opposite of mitigate.
656936127.whyC: Finish means to end completely; mitigate means to lessen, not eliminate.
656936127.explanationTl: Ang 'mitigate' ay bawasan ang bigat o sakit ng isang bagay, kaya kapareho ng 'alleviate'.
656936127.hintTl: Trabaho ng doktor na bawasan ang paghihirap ng tao.

791723399.hint: A plumber who lacks this quality would overcharge you. What is missing?
791723399.whyA: Afraid is about fear; the sentence is about care and honesty in the work.
791723399.whyB: Employed refers to having a job, not to how carefully or honestly one works.
791723399.whyD: Infamous means having a bad reputation, which does not fit 'less ___'.
791723399.explanationTl: Ang 'scrupulous' ay maingat at may konsensya sa trabaho; ang 'less scrupulous' na plumber ay mandadaya, kaya 'careful' ang pinakamalapit.
791723399.hintTl: Ang plumber na kulang dito ay magpapamahal ng singil. Anong ugali ang wala sa kanya?

1050194713.whyA: Slowly is the opposite of rapidly.
1050194713.whyC: Quietly fits a rumor but describes sound, not speed.
1050194713.whyD: Secretly fits a rumor but describes hiddenness, not speed.
1050194713.explanationTl: Ang 'rapidly' ay mabilis, kaya 'quickly' ang sagot.

1136400058.hint: How would residents feel when the power suddenly goes out?
1136400058.whyB: Deliberation means careful thought, not a sudden feeling of alarm.
1136400058.whyC: Disability is a physical or mental limitation, unrelated to a reaction.
1136400058.whyD: Distaste is dislike, not the alarm and confusion a blackout causes.
1136400058.explanationTl: Ang 'consternation' ay pagkabahala o pagkagulat na may halong pagkalito, kaya 'dismay' ang pinakamalapit.
1136400058.hintTl: Ano ang mararamdaman ng mga residente kapag biglang nag-brownout?

1360294987.whyA: Planned is the opposite; fortuitous events happen by chance.
1360294987.whyC: Unfortunate means unlucky, the opposite of the usual sense of fortuitous.
1360294987.whyD: Deliberate means done on purpose, the opposite of happening by chance.
1360294987.explanationTl: Ang 'fortuitous' ay nangyari nang hindi sinasadya pero kadalasan ay swerte, kaya 'lucky' ang sagot.
1360294987.hintTl: Pansinin mo ang 'fortune' sa loob ng salita.

1405879297.hint: A pragmatic person asks, 'Will it actually work?'
1405879297.whyA: Idealistic is the opposite: focused on ideals rather than what works.
1405879297.whyC: Stubborn means unwilling to change one's mind, not focused on practicality.
1405879297.whyD: Talkative is about how much someone speaks, unrelated to being practical.
1405879297.explanationTl: Ang 'pragmatic' ay praktikal, tumitingin sa kung ano ang talagang gumagana, kaya 'practical' ang sagot.
1405879297.hintTl: Ang pragmatic na tao ay nagtatanong, 'Gagana ba talaga ito?'

1511850923.text: In the sentence 'The light is on,' the word 'light' most nearly means:
1511850923.explanation: A light that can be 'on' is a lamp or bulb, so 'light' here means illumination.
1511850923.hint: What kind of light can be switched on?
1511850923.whyA: 'Not heavy' is the adjective sense of light, which cannot be switched on.
1511850923.whyC: 'Pale in color' (as in light blue) is another adjective sense that does not fit 'is on'.
1511850923.whyD: 'Gentle or soft' (as in a light touch) does not fit something that is switched on.
1511850923.explanationTl: Ang light na puwedeng 'on' ay ilaw o bombilya, kaya 'illumination' ang ibig sabihin dito.
1511850923.hintTl: Anong klaseng light ang puwedeng i-switch on?

1961119059.hint: Something ubiquitous seems to be found everywhere you look.
1961119059.whyA: Rare is the opposite of ubiquitous.
1961119059.whyC: Unique means one of a kind, close to the opposite of being everywhere.
1961119059.whyD: Obscure means little known or hidden, not present everywhere.
1961119059.explanationTl: Ang 'ubiquitous' ay nasa lahat ng lugar, kaya kapareho ng 'omnipresent'.
1961119059.hintTl: Ang ubiquitous ay parang nakikita mo kahit saan ka tumingin.

2144520768.explanation: 'Feasible' means able to be done or carried out, so 'possible' is the closest meaning.
2144520768.hint: Ask: can the plan actually be carried out?
2144520768.whyA: Impossible is the opposite of feasible.
2144520768.whyC: Expensive is about cost; a plan can be costly and still feasible.
2144520768.whyD: Popular means well-liked, not able to be done.
2144520768.explanationTl: Ang 'feasible' ay kayang gawin o maisakatuparan, kaya 'possible' ang sagot.
2144520768.hintTl: Itanong mo: kaya ba talagang gawin ang plano?

292186588.explanation: A compass is the tool whose main purpose is navigating; a ruler is the tool whose main purpose is measuring.
292186588.hint: Ask: what is each tool mainly made for?
292186588.whyB: A ruler is not used for writing; that is a pen or pencil.
292186588.whyC: Cutting is done with scissors or a cutter; a ruler only guides the cut.
292186588.whyD: Aligning is a side use; the ruler's main job is measuring length.
292186588.explanationTl: Ang compass ay ginagamit para mag-navigate, at ang ruler naman ay pangunahing ginagamit para mag-measure.
292186588.hintTl: Isipin mo: para saan talaga ginawa ang bawat tool?

538271447.explanation: Hertz is the SI unit of frequency, and the meter is the SI unit of length.
538271447.hint: Match each quantity with the unit used to measure it.
538271447.explanationTl: Ang unit ng frequency ay hertz, at ang unit ng length ay meter.
538271447.hintTl: I-match ang bawat quantity sa unit na ginagamit para i-measure ito.

637008230.explanation: A ruler measures length, and a weighing scale measures weight.
637008230.whyB: Height is a kind of length, so it goes with the ruler, not the scale.
637008230.whyC: Volume is measured with a measuring cup or graduated cylinder.
637008230.whyD: Area is computed from lengths; a scale does not measure it.
637008230.explanationTl: Ang ruler ay pang-measure ng length, at ang timbangan (scale) ay pang-measure ng weight.
637008230.hintTl: Ano ang sinusukat ng bawat instrument?

997900159.text: Pen is to writer as brush is to:
997900159.explanation: A pen is the main tool of a writer, and a brush is the main tool of a painter.
997900159.hint: Whose main tool is a brush?
997900159.whyB: A sculptor mainly uses a chisel or clay tools, not a brush.
997900159.whyC: A carpenter mainly uses a hammer and saw.
997900159.whyD: A photographer mainly uses a camera.
997900159.explanationTl: Ang pen ang pangunahing gamit ng writer, at ang brush naman ang pangunahing gamit ng painter.

1189549097.explanation: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge, and the second is the SI unit of time.
1189549097.hint: Match each quantity with its unit.
1189549097.explanationTl: Ang unit ng electric charge ay coulomb, at ang unit ng time ay second.
1189549097.hintTl: I-match ang bawat quantity sa unit nito.

1387077245.text: Oven is to baking as refrigerator is to:
1387077245.explanation: An oven is used for baking, and a refrigerator is used for cooling food.
1387077245.hint: What is the main job of each appliance?
1387077245.whyB: Heating is the opposite of what a refrigerator does.
1387077245.whyC: Drying is the job of a dryer or the sun, not a refrigerator.
1387077245.whyD: Washing is the job of a washing machine.
1387077245.explanationTl: Ang oven ay pang-bake, at ang ref naman ay pampalamig ng pagkain.
1387077245.hintTl: Ano ang pangunahing trabaho ng bawat appliance?

1572436242.text: Negligent is to care as dishonest is to:
1572436242.explanation: A negligent person lacks care, and a dishonest person lacks truthfulness.
1572436242.hint: Each word describes a person who is missing a certain quality.
1572436242.whyB: Lacking generosity describes a stingy person, not a dishonest one.
1572436242.whyD: Lacking patience describes an impatient person.
1572436242.explanationTl: Ang negligent na tao ay kulang sa care, at ang dishonest na tao ay kulang sa truthfulness.
1572436242.hintTl: Ang bawat salita ay naglalarawan ng taong kulang sa isang katangian.

2022670371.explanation: A downpour is a much stronger form of a drizzle, just as a gale is a much stronger form of a breeze.
2022670371.hint: Look at how strong the second word is compared with the first.
2022670371.whyB: Rain comes from a cloud; that is source, not degree.
2022670371.whyC: Snow and ice are different forms of frozen water, not weak and strong versions of one thing.
2022670371.whyD: Thunder and lightning happen together; one is not a stronger form of the other.
2022670371.explanationTl: Ang downpour ay mas malakas na version ng drizzle, gaya ng gale na mas malakas na version ng breeze.
2022670371.hintTl: Tingnan kung gaano kalakas ang pangalawang salita kumpara sa una.

1918022796.text: Statement: "Join our weekend review classes to pass the Civil Service Exam." Which of the following is assumed in the statement?
1918022796.optionA: The review classes help examinees pass the exam.
1918022796.optionB: Everyone who joins the classes will surely pass.
1918022796.optionC: The exam is given only on weekends.
1918022796.optionD: Examinees who do not join will surely fail.
1918022796.explanation: The advice only makes sense if the speaker believes the review classes help people pass; that unstated belief is the assumption.
1918022796.hint: What must the speaker believe for the advice to make sense?
1918022796.whyB: The statement does not promise that every attendee will pass; that goes too far.
1918022796.whyC: The classes are on weekends, but nothing is said about when the exam is held.
1918022796.whyD: The statement does not say the classes are the only way to pass.
1918022796.explanationTl: May sense lang ang advice kung naniniwala ang nagsabi na nakakatulong ang review classes para pumasa. Iyon ang assumption.
1918022796.hintTl: Ano ang kailangang paniwalaan ng nagsasalita para may sense ang advice niya?

145369577.explanation: Each value equals n^2 + 3n: 1 + 3 = 4, 4 + 6 = 10, 9 + 9 = 18, so 4 gives 16 + 12 = 28.
145369577.steps:
1. Check the gaps: 10 - 4 = 6, 18 - 10 = 8; the gaps grow by 2.
2. The next gap is 10.
3. 18 + 10 = 28.
4. Check with n^2 + 3n: 4 x 4 + 3 x 4 = 16 + 12 = 28.
145369577.hint: Look at the gaps between the values on the right.
145369577.whyA: 26 adds 8 again instead of letting the gap grow to 10.
145369577.whyB: 27 fits neither the gap pattern nor n^2 + 3n.
145369577.explanationTl: Ang bawat value ay n^2 + 3n. Kaya para sa 4: 16 + 12 = 28.
145369577.stepsTl:
1. Tingnan ang pagitan: 6, tapos 8. Lumalaki ng 2.
2. Kaya ang susunod na pagitan ay 10.
3. 18 + 10 = 28.
4. I-check gamit ang n^2 + 3n: 16 + 12 = 28.
145369577.hintTl: Tingnan ang pagitan ng mga value sa kanan.

694184605.text: A barangay health center recorded its visitors for three days: Day 1, 150; Day 2, 200; Day 3, 250. What is the average number of visitors per day?
694184605.steps:
1. Add the visitors: 150 + 200 + 250 = 600.
2. Divide by the number of days: 600 / 3 = 200.
694184605.hint: Add all the values, then divide by how many days there are.
694184605.whyA: 190 is a miscalculation; the total 600 divided by 3 is exactly 200.
694184605.whyC: 210 is too high; the values are evenly spaced, so the average is the middle value.
694184605.whyD: 220 is too high; it leans toward the largest value instead of the middle.
694184605.explanationTl: I-add lahat: 150 + 200 + 250 = 600. Tapos i-divide sa 3 days, kaya 200.
694184605.stepsTl:
1. I-add ang visitors: 150 + 200 + 250 = 600.
2. I-divide sa bilang ng araw: 600 / 3 = 200.
694184605.hintTl: I-add lahat ng value, tapos i-divide sa bilang ng araw.

1988342223.text: A sari-sari store recorded its sales: Monday, P1,200; Tuesday, P1,500; Wednesday, P1,800. By what percent did sales increase from Monday to Wednesday?
1988342223.steps:
1. Increase: 1,800 - 1,200 = 600.
2. Divide by the starting value (Monday): 600 / 1,200 = 0.5.
3. Convert to percent: 0.5 x 100 = 50%.
1988342223.hint: Percent increase = increase divided by the starting value.
1988342223.whyA: 25% is the increase from Monday to Tuesday only (300 / 1,200).
1988342223.whyC: 33 1/3% divides the increase by Wednesday's sales (600 / 1,800) instead of Monday's.
1988342223.whyD: 150% is Wednesday's sales as a percent of Monday's (1,800 / 1,200), not the increase.
1988342223.explanationTl: Ang itinaas ng sales ay P600. I-divide sa P1,200 (starting value), kaya 0.5 o 50%.
1988342223.stepsTl:
1. Increase: 1,800 - 1,200 = 600.
2. I-divide sa starting value (Monday): 600 / 1,200 = 0.5.
3. Gawing percent: 0.5 x 100 = 50%.
1988342223.hintTl: Percent increase = increase na hinati sa starting value.

1507188177.explanation: Oak, pine and maple are trees, while a rose is a flowering shrub.
1507188177.hint: Think about what kind of plant each one is.
1507188177.whyA: Oak is a tree, like pine and maple.
1507188177.whyB: Pine is a cone-bearing tree, but it is still a tree like oak and maple.
1507188177.whyC: Maple is a tree, like oak and pine.
1507188177.explanationTl: Ang oak, pine at maple ay mga puno, pero ang rose ay halamang namumulaklak (shrub).
1507188177.hintTl: Isipin kung anong klaseng halaman ang bawat isa.

283642176.whyA: 44 adds 9 again instead of the next gap of 10.
283642176.whyD: 47 adds 12; the gaps grow by only 1.
283642176.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ay 7, 8, 9, kaya ang susunod ay 10. 35 + 10 = 45.

583791673.whyA: 28 adds 7 again instead of the next gap of 8.
583791673.whyD: 31 adds 10; the gaps grow by only 1.
583791673.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ay 5, 6, 7, kaya ang susunod ay 8. 21 + 8 = 29.

690156220.explanation: Each term is double the previous term minus 1 (the gaps 3, 6, 12 double), so 25 x 2 - 1 = 49.
690156220.steps:
1. The gaps are 3, 6, 12; each gap doubles.
2. The next gap is 24.
3. 25 + 24 = 49.
4. Check: each term = previous x 2 - 1, and 25 x 2 - 1 = 49.
690156220.hint: Look at the gaps. Are they growing by adding or by multiplying?
690156220.whyA: 37 adds 12 again instead of doubling the gap to 24.
690156220.explanationTl: Ang bawat term ay doble ng nauna minus 1. Kaya 25 x 2 - 1 = 49.
690156220.stepsTl:
1. Ang pagitan ay 3, 6, 12. Dumodoble.
2. Kaya ang susunod na pagitan ay 24.
3. 25 + 24 = 49.
4. I-check: nauna x 2 - 1, kaya 25 x 2 - 1 = 49.
690156220.hintTl: Tingnan ang pagitan. Nagdadagdag ba o nagmu-multiply?

1242023609.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the three branches of the Philippine government are:
1242023609.explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), executive power in the President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
1242023609.hint: Think of who makes the laws, who carries them out, and who interprets them.
1242023609.whyB: Elections are run by the COMELEC, a constitutional commission, not a separate branch of government.
1242023609.whyC: The Constitutional Commissions (Art. IX) are independent bodies, not one of the three branches; the Executive is missing.
1242023609.whyD: Local governments (Art. X) are political subdivisions, not a branch; the Legislative is missing.
1242023609.explanationTl: Sa 1987 Constitution, ang legislative power ay nasa Congress (Art. VI, Sec. 1), ang executive power ay nasa President (Art. VII, Sec. 1), at ang judicial power ay nasa Supreme Court at lower courts (Art. VIII, Sec. 1). Kaya tatlo: Executive, Legislative, Judicial.
1242023609.hintTl: Isipin mo: sino ang gumagawa ng batas, sino ang nagpapatupad, at sino ang nag-i-interpret?

1932774891.explanation: Art. XIV, Sec. 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which is to be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
1932774891.hint: The Constitution names a language that is still being developed from many Philippine languages, not just one regional language.
1932774891.whyA: Tagalog is the main base of Filipino, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog, as the national language.
1932774891.whyC: English is an official language (with Filipino) for communication and instruction under Art. XIV, Sec. 7, not the national language.
1932774891.whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
1932774891.explanationTl: Ayon sa Art. XIV, Sec. 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Base ito sa Tagalog pero dine-develop pa gamit ang ibang Philippine languages, kaya hindi 'Tagalog' ang tamang sagot.
1932774891.hintTl: Hindi lang isang regional language ang pinangalanan ng Constitution, kundi isang language na patuloy na dine-develop.

33206014.hint: It is the ocean on the eastern side of the Philippines.
33206014.whyA: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean, about half the size of the Pacific.
33206014.whyB: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest ocean.
33206014.whyD: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest of the major oceans.
33206014.explanationTl: Pacific Ocean ang pinakamalaki at pinakamalalim na ocean, halos one-third ng surface ng Earth. Ito rin ang ocean sa silangan ng Pilipinas.
33206014.hintTl: Ito yung ocean na nasa silangang side ng Pilipinas.

354291116.hint: It is the simplest hydrocarbon, with only one carbon atom.
354291116.whyB: Ethane (two carbons) is present in natural gas only in smaller amounts.
354291116.whyC: Propane is a minor part of natural gas; it is the main gas in LPG.
354291116.whyD: Butane is a minor part of natural gas; it is mixed with propane in LPG tanks.
354291116.explanationTl: Methane (CH4) ang pangunahing component ng natural gas. Ang propane at butane naman ang laman ng LPG na ginagamit sa bahay.
354291116.hintTl: Ito yung pinakasimpleng hydrocarbon, isang carbon atom lang.

379682279.text: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity through which effect?
379682279.explanation: Solar cells use the photovoltaic effect: light striking a semiconductor such as silicon frees electrons and produces an electric current.
379682279.hint: The name joins the Greek word for light with the unit of electric potential.
379682279.whyA: The greenhouse effect is the trapping of heat by gases in the atmosphere; it does not generate electricity.
379682279.whyC: The piezoelectric effect produces electricity from mechanical pressure, not from light.
379682279.whyD: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency of a wave from a moving source; it has nothing to do with electricity.
379682279.explanationTl: Photovoltaic effect ang ginagamit ng solar cells: pag tinamaan ng liwanag ang semiconductor tulad ng silicon, may electrons na nare-release at nagkakaroon ng electric current.
379682279.hintTl: Pinagsama sa pangalan ang Greek word para sa 'light' at ang unit ng electric potential.

602591236.explanation: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm, larger than Earth, that has been observed continuously since the 1800s.
602591236.hint: It is the largest planet in the Solar System.
602591236.whyA: Mars is called the Red Planet because of its rusty soil, but it has no Great Red Spot.
602591236.whyC: Saturn is known for its rings; its storms are not called the Great Red Spot.
602591236.whyD: Venus is covered by thick yellowish clouds and has no Great Red Spot.
602591236.explanationTl: Ang Great Red Spot ay isang napakalaking storm sa Jupiter, mas malaki pa sa Earth, at nakikita na ito ng mga astronomer mula pa noong 1800s.
602591236.hintTl: Ito ang pinakamalaking planet sa Solar System.

754206978.hint: Pakistan, Nepal and Sri Lanka use currencies with the same name.
754206978.whyB: The ruble is the currency of Russia.
754206978.whyC: The yen is the currency of Japan.
754206978.whyD: The dollar is used by the United States and several other countries, not India.
754206978.explanationTl: Rupee ang official currency ng India. Ang ruble ay sa Russia at ang yen ay sa Japan, kaya huwag malito sa magkakahawig na pangalan.
754206978.hintTl: Ganito rin ang pangalan ng currency ng Pakistan, Nepal at Sri Lanka.

758915308.text: In oxy-fuel welding and cutting, which gas is commonly burned with oxygen as the fuel?
758915308.explanation: Acetylene burned with pure oxygen gives the hottest common fuel-gas flame (over 3,000 °C), hot enough to melt steel, so it is the standard fuel in oxy-fuel welding.
758915308.hint: Only one option is a gas that can burn.
758915308.whyA: Nitrogen does not burn; it is mostly inert and is used for purging, not as a fuel.
758915308.whyC: Argon is an inert shielding gas used in TIG and MIG welding; it cannot burn.
758915308.whyD: Carbon dioxide is a shielding gas in MIG welding; it is already fully burned and cannot be a fuel.
758915308.explanationTl: Acetylene ang fuel gas sa oxy-fuel welding. Pag sinunog ito kasama ng pure oxygen, umaabot sa mahigit 3,000 °C ang flame, sapat para matunaw ang steel.
758915308.hintTl: Isa lang sa mga choices ang gas na nasusunog.

764249826.hint: It is in the city of Agra, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
764249826.whyB: Pakistan has Mughal monuments like the Badshahi Mosque, but not the Taj Mahal.
764249826.whyC: Bangladesh is a neighbor of India but the Taj Mahal is not there.
764249826.whyD: Nepal is known for Mount Everest and Himalayan temples, not the Taj Mahal.
764249826.explanationTl: Ang Taj Mahal ay nasa Agra, India. Pinagawa ito ni Mughal emperor Shah Jahan para sa asawa niya, at UNESCO World Heritage Site na ito.
764249826.hintTl: Nasa Agra ito, pinagawa ni Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

1263506978.explanation: Mount Everest, on the Nepal-China border in the Himalayas, is the highest mountain above sea level at about 8,849 meters.
1263506978.hint: It is named after a British surveyor and sits on the Nepal-China border.
1263506978.whyA: K2 is the second-highest mountain, about 240 m lower than Everest.
1263506978.whyD: Lhotse is the fourth-highest and is right next to Everest, which is why it gets confused with it.
1263506978.explanationTl: Mount Everest ang pinakamataas na bundok sa mundo, mga 8,849 meters above sea level. Nasa Himalayas ito, sa border ng Nepal at China.
1263506978.hintTl: Ipinangalan ito sa isang British surveyor, at nasa border ng Nepal at China.

1301197882.hint: Its deepest point is the Challenger Deep, near Guam.
1301197882.whyA: The Tonga Trench is the second-deepest, about 10,800 m, slightly shallower.
1301197882.whyC: The Philippine Trench, east of Mindanao, is about 10,500 m deep, among the deepest but not the deepest.
1301197882.whyD: The Kermadec Trench is very deep (about 10,000 m) but shallower than the Mariana Trench.
1301197882.explanationTl: Mariana Trench ang pinakamalalim na trench sa mundo, mga 11,000 meters. Ang deepest point nito ay ang Challenger Deep malapit sa Guam. Malalim din ang Philippine Trench pero hindi siya ang pinakamalalim.
1301197882.hintTl: Nandito ang Challenger Deep, malapit sa Guam.

1689606369.hint: This country spans both Eastern Europe and northern Asia.
1689606369.whyA: Canada is the second-largest country, about 10 million square kilometers.
1689606369.whyC: China is about 9.6 million square kilometers, much smaller than the largest.
1689606369.whyD: The United States is about 9.8 million square kilometers, also much smaller.
1689606369.explanationTl: Russia ang pinakamalaking bansa, mga 17.1 million square kilometers, at sakop nito ang Eastern Europe at northern Asia. Pangalawa lang ang Canada.
1689606369.hintTl: Sakop ng bansang ito ang Eastern Europe at northern Asia.

1994483470.hint: The Kremlin and Red Square are in this city.
1994483470.whyB: St. Petersburg was the capital in the imperial era (1712-1918) but is no longer the capital.
1994483470.whyC: Kazan is a major city and capital of Tatarstan, not of Russia.
1994483470.whyD: Novosibirsk is the largest city in Siberia, not the national capital.
1994483470.explanationTl: Moscow ang capital ng Russia, dito makikita ang Kremlin at Red Square. Naging capital ang St. Petersburg noong panahon ng mga Tsar, pero hindi na ngayon.
1994483470.hintTl: Nandito ang Kremlin at Red Square.

2115698073.hint: The Celsius scale was set so that water freezes at 0 and boils at a round number.
2115698073.whyA: 50 °C is only hot water; it is half the boiling point.
2115698073.whyC: 150 °C is above boiling; water at sea level cannot get that hot as a liquid in an open pot.
2115698073.whyD: 200 °C is a typical oven temperature, not the boiling point of water.
2115698073.explanationTl: Sa sea level, kumukulo ang tubig sa 100 °C. Sa matataas na lugar, mas mababa ang pressure kaya mas mababa rin ang boiling point.
2115698073.hintTl: Sa Celsius scale, 0 ang freezing ng tubig at round number ang boiling.

367111671.text: Intramuros, known as the 'Walled City', is located in which Philippine city?
367111671.explanation: Intramuros, the Spanish-era fortified district surrounded by stone walls, is in the City of Manila; its name means 'within the walls'.
367111671.hint: It was the seat of Spanish colonial government, beside the Pasig River.
367111671.whyA: Vigan is famous for its Spanish-era heritage street (Calle Crisologo), but it is not the Walled City.
367111671.whyC: Cebu has Fort San Pedro, a small fort, not the Walled City.
367111671.whyD: Davao was never a walled Spanish city.
367111671.explanationTl: Ang Intramuros, ibig sabihin 'within the walls', ay nasa City of Manila. Ito ang napapaderang lungsod noong panahon ng Kastila at sentro ng gobyerno nila.
367111671.hintTl: Ito ang sentro ng gobyerno ng mga Kastila, katabi ng Pasig River.

1489654682.text: Philippine Independence Day is celebrated every:
1489654682.explanation: Independence Day marks the proclamation of Philippine independence from Spain by Emilio Aguinaldo in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898. The celebration was moved from July 4 to June 12 in 1962 and fixed by Republic Act No. 4166 (1964).
1489654682.hint: Think of the 1898 proclamation in Kawit, Cavite.
1489654682.whyB: July 4 is when the US recognized Philippine independence in 1946; it was celebrated as Independence Day only until 1961 and was renamed Republic Day.
1489654682.whyC: August 31 is not Philippine Independence Day; National Heroes Day falls on the last Monday of August.
1489654682.whyD: April 9 is Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valor), commemorating the Fall of Bataan in 1942.
1489654682.explanationTl: June 12 ang Independence Day natin, kasi noong June 12, 1898 dineklara ni Emilio Aguinaldo ang independence mula sa Spain sa Kawit, Cavite. Dati July 4 ang celebration, pero inilipat sa June 12 noong 1962 at ginawang batas ng RA 4166 noong 1964.
1489654682.hintTl: Alalahanin mo ang proclamation sa Kawit, Cavite noong 1898.

440919046.steps:
1. "Sum" means the result of adding.
2. Add 9 to x: x + 9.
440919046.hint: Which operation does the word "sum" stand for?
440919046.whyA: x − 9 is the difference of x and 9, not the sum.
440919046.whyB: x9 means x times 9 (a product), not a sum.
440919046.whyD: x/9 is the quotient of x and 9, not the sum.
440919046.explanationTl: Ang "sum" ay ibig sabihin addition, kaya ang sagot ay x + 9.
440919046.stepsTl:
1. Ang "sum" ay resulta ng pag-add.
2. I-add ang 9 sa x: x + 9.
440919046.hintTl: Anong operation ang ibig sabihin ng salitang "sum"?

929664260.text: If a = b × c, b = 10 and c = 2, what is a?
929664260.steps:
1. Replace b with 10 and c with 2.
2. a = 10 × 2 = 20.
929664260.stepsTl:
1. Palitan ang b ng 10 at ang c ng 2.
2. a = 10 × 2 = 20.
929664260.whyB: 12 adds b and c (10 + 2) instead of multiplying.

1291586413.text: If r = s + t, s = 4 and t = 6, what is r?
1291586413.steps:
1. Replace s with 4 and t with 6.
2. r = 4 + 6 = 10.
1291586413.stepsTl:
1. Palitan ang s ng 4 at ang t ng 6.
2. r = 4 + 6 = 10.
1291586413.whyC: 8 is a slip in the addition; 4 + 6 = 10.
1291586413.whyD: 12 is a slip in the addition; 4 + 6 = 10.

1318363438.explanation: Subtract 3 from both sides to get 3x = 9, then divide by 3: x = 3.
1318363438.explanationTl: Ibawas ang 3 sa magkabilang side para 3x = 9, tapos i-divide sa 3: x = 3.
1318363438.stepsTl:
1. Ibawas ang 3 sa magkabilang side: 3x = 9.
2. Hatiin sa 3: x = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
Check: 3(3) + 3 = 12 ✓

1383073297.text: If a = 2b − c, b = 6 and c = 9, what is a?
1383073297.steps:
1. Replace b with 6 and c with 9: a = 2(6) − 9.
2. Multiply first: 2 × 6 = 12.
3. Subtract: 12 − 9 = 3.
1383073297.hint: Substitute, then multiply before you subtract.
1383073297.whyA: 21 adds c (12 + 9) instead of subtracting it.
1383073297.stepsTl:
1. Palitan ang b ng 6 at ang c ng 9: a = 2(6) − 9.
2. Multiply muna: 2 × 6 = 12.
3. I-subtract: 12 − 9 = 3.
1383073297.hintTl: I-substitute, tapos unahin ang multiplication bago mag-subtract.

1907526426.steps:
1. x is divided by 4, so undo it by multiplying both sides by 4.
2. x = 5 × 4 = 20.
Check: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 ✓
1907526426.hint: Undo the division by doing the opposite operation.
1907526426.explanationTl: I-multiply ang magkabilang side sa 4: x = 5 × 4 = 20.
1907526426.stepsTl:
1. Divided by 4 ang x, kaya i-multiply sa 4 ang magkabilang side.
2. x = 5 × 4 = 20.
Check: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 ✓
1907526426.hintTl: I-undo ang division gamit ang kabaligtarang operation.

70033427.whyB: 0.05 is 5/100 — the decimal point moved one place too far.
70033427.whyC: 5.0 is just the numerator; it ignores dividing by 10.

338613393.steps:
1. Divide the numerator by the denominator: 13 ÷ 16.
2. 13.0000 ÷ 16 = 0.8125.
Check: 0.8125 × 16 = 13 ✓
338613393.hint: A fraction bar means "divided by" — top divided by bottom.
338613393.whyA: 0.08125 puts the decimal point one place too far left.
338613393.stepsTl:
1. I-divide ang numerator sa denominator: 13 ÷ 16.
2. 13.0000 ÷ 16 = 0.8125.
Check: 0.8125 × 16 = 13 ✓
338613393.hintTl: Ang fraction bar ay "divided by" — itaas hinati sa ibaba.

878196308.explanation: Same denominators, so subtract the numerators: 4 − 1 = 3, giving 3/7.
878196308.steps:
1. The denominators are already the same (7).
2. Subtract the numerators: 4 − 1 = 3.
3. Keep the denominator: 3/7.
878196308.hint: When the denominators match, work only with the numerators.
878196308.whyB: 5/7 adds the numerators instead of subtracting.
878196308.whyD: 1/7 is just the fraction being subtracted, not the result.
878196308.explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya i-subtract lang ang numerators: 4 − 1 = 3, so 3/7.
878196308.stepsTl:
1. Pareho na ang denominator (7).
2. I-subtract ang numerators: 4 − 1 = 3.
3. Panatilihin ang denominator: 3/7.
878196308.hintTl: Kapag pareho ang denominator, numerators lang ang gagalawin.

1089880767.explanation: Same denominators, so add the numerators: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4, which simplifies to 1/2.
1089880767.steps:
1. The denominators are the same (4).
2. Add the numerators: 1 + 1 = 2, so 2/4.
3. Simplify: 2/4 = 1/2.
1089880767.hint: When the denominators match, add only the numerators, then simplify.
1089880767.whyB: 1/4 is just one of the addends; adding gives more than that.
1089880767.whyC: 2/8 adds the denominators too; only the numerators are added.
1089880767.explanationTl: Pareho ang denominator, kaya i-add lang ang numerators: 2/4, na pwedeng i-simplify sa 1/2.
1089880767.stepsTl:
1. Pareho ang denominator (4).
2. I-add ang numerators: 1 + 1 = 2, so 2/4.
3. I-simplify: 2/4 = 1/2.
1089880767.hintTl: Kapag pareho ang denominator, numerators lang ang i-add, tapos i-simplify.

1433273404.text: What is the area of a triangle with a base of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm?
1433273404.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm².
1433273404.steps:
1. Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.
2. 6 × 8 = 48.
3. ½ × 48 = 24 cm².
1433273404.hint: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.
1433273404.whyA: 48 cm² forgets to take half (that is the rectangle's area).
1433273404.whyC: 32 cm² does not follow from ½ × 6 × 8.
1433273404.whyD: 40 cm² does not follow from ½ × 6 × 8.
1433273404.explanationTl: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm².
1433273404.stepsTl:
1. Area ng triangle = ½ × base × height.
2. 6 × 8 = 48.
3. ½ × 48 = 24 cm².
1433273404.hintTl: Ang triangle ay kalahati ng rectangle na may parehong base at height.

1486412531.text: A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 5 m wide. How many meters of fencing are needed to go around it?
1486412531.steps:
1. Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + width).
2. 12 + 5 = 17.
3. 2 × 17 = 34 m.
1486412531.hint: Going around means adding all four sides, not just two.
1486412531.whyA: 17 m adds only one length and one width.
1486412531.whyB: 60 m multiplies length by width — that is the area, not the fence.
1486412531.whyD: 29 m counts the length twice but the width only once.
1486412531.hintTl: Paikot ang bakod, kaya apat na sides ang i-add, hindi dalawa lang.

1582492509.text: What is the volume of a cube with a side of 3 cm?
1582492509.steps:
1. Volume of a cube = side³.
2. 3 × 3 = 9.
3. 9 × 3 = 27 cm³.
1582492509.hint: A cube has the same length, width and height — multiply all three.
1582492509.whyB: 9 cm³ is side² — the area of one face, not the volume.
1582492509.hintTl: Pare-pareho ang haba, lapad at taas ng cube — i-multiply ang tatlo.

425277101.text: A book priced at ₱250 is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
425277101.explanation: 20% of ₱250 = ₱50, so the sale price is ₱250 − ₱50 = ₱200.
425277101.explanationTl: Ang 20% ng ₱250 ay ₱50, kaya ₱250 − ₱50 = ₱200 ang babayaran.

734121756.text: A watch priced at ₱2,000 is sold at a 25% discount. What is the sale price?
734121756.explanationTl: Ang 25% ng ₱2,000 ay ₱500, kaya ₱2,000 − ₱500 = ₱1,500 ang babayaran.

1326332900.text: A pair of shoes priced at ₱1,000 is sold at a 50% discount. What is the sale price?
1326332900.explanationTl: Ang 50% ng ₱1,000 ay ₱500, kaya ₱1,000 − ₱500 = ₱500 ang babayaran.

1338857299.text: A necklace priced at ₱2,500 is sold at a 10% discount. What is the sale price?
1338857299.explanationTl: Ang 10% ng ₱2,500 ay ₱250, kaya ₱2,500 − ₱250 = ₱2,250 ang babayaran.

1630710049.text: After a 10% discount, a book costs ₱180. What was its original price?
1630710049.explanation: ₱180 is 90% of the original price, so the original price = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
1630710049.steps:
1. After a 10% discount you pay 90% of the price.
2. 0.9 × original = ₱180.
3. Original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
Check: 10% of ₱200 = ₱20; ₱200 − ₱20 = ₱180 ✓
1630710049.hint: ₱180 is what percent of the original price?
1630710049.whyA: ₱198 adds 10% of ₱180; the 10% was taken from the original price, not from ₱180.
1630710049.whyB: ₱190 just adds ₱10 back; the discount was ₱20.
1630710049.whyC: ₱162 takes another 10% off ₱180 instead of going back to the original.
1630710049.explanationTl: Ang ₱180 ay 90% ng original price, kaya original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
1630710049.stepsTl:
1. Kapag 10% ang discount, 90% lang ng presyo ang binabayaran.
2. 0.9 × original = ₱180.
3. Original = 180 ÷ 0.9 = ₱200.
Check: 10% ng ₱200 = ₱20; ₱200 − ₱20 = ₱180 ✓
1630710049.hintTl: Ilang percent ng original price ang ₱180?

1840313242.text: A smartphone priced at ₱15,000 is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
1840313242.whyB: ₱13,000 subtracts only ₱2,000 — a slip in computing 20% of ₱15,000 (it is ₱3,000).
1840313242.whyC: ₱11,000 subtracts ₱4,000, more than the 20% discount of ₱3,000.

1882087395.hint: Divide the part by the whole, then change the decimal to a percent.
1882087395.whyA: 40% is a guess from 120 ÷ 30 = 4 with the decimal misplaced; 30 ÷ 120 = 0.25.
1882087395.whyB: 4% comes from 120 ÷ 30 — whole divided by part.
1882087395.whyD: 30% just reuses the number 30 from the question.
1882087395.hintTl: I-divide ang part sa whole, tapos gawing percent.

263928250.text: A boat travels 90 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
263928250.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 90 km ÷ 3 h = 30 km/h.
263928250.whyB: 20 km/h would cover only 60 km in 3 hours.
263928250.whyC: 40 km/h would cover 120 km in 3 hours.
263928250.whyD: 50 km/h would cover 150 km in 3 hours.

1520624502.text: A jeepney travels 45 km in 1 hour and 30 minutes. What is its average speed in km/h?
1520624502.explanation: 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours, so speed = 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.
1520624502.steps:
1. Convert the time: 30 minutes = 0.5 hour, so 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h.
2. Speed = distance ÷ time = 45 ÷ 1.5.
3. 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.
1520624502.hint: Change the minutes into a fraction of an hour first.
1520624502.whyB: 35 km/h treats 1 h 30 min as 1.3 hours (45 ÷ 1.3 ≈ 35).
1520624502.whyC: 15 km/h divides 45 by 3, treating 1 h 30 min as 3 hours.
1520624502.explanationTl: Ang 1 hour 30 minutes ay 1.5 hours, kaya 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.
1520624502.stepsTl:
1. I-convert ang oras: 30 minutes = 0.5 hour, so 1.5 h.
2. Speed = layo ÷ oras = 45 ÷ 1.5.
3. 45 ÷ 1.5 = 30 km/h.
1520624502.hintTl: Gawin munang hours ang minutes bago mag-divide.

1802624888.text: A drone flies 40 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
1802624888.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 40 km ÷ 2 h = 20 km/h.
1802624888.whyB: 30 km/h would cover 60 km in 2 hours.
1802624888.whyD: 40 km/h is the distance, not the speed — it forgets to divide by the time.

1874609057.text: A boat travels 12 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
1874609057.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 12 km ÷ 2 h = 6 km/h.
1874609057.whyB: 5 km/h would cover only 10 km in 2 hours.
1874609057.whyC: 7 km/h would cover 14 km in 2 hours.
1874609057.whyD: 8 km/h would cover 16 km in 2 hours.

2121797046.text: A train travels 300 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
2121797046.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 300 km ÷ 5 h = 60 km/h.
2121797046.whyB: 50 km/h would cover only 250 km in 5 hours.
2121797046.whyC: 70 km/h would cover 350 km in 5 hours.
2121797046.whyD: 40 km/h would cover only 200 km in 5 hours.

273930774.explanation: Each term goes up by 3, so 12 + 3 = 15.
273930774.text: What is the next number in the series: 3, 6, 9, 12, ...?

427974349.explanation: The gaps grow by 1 (+1, +2, +3, +4), so the next gap is 5: 11 + 5 = 16.
427974349.explanationTl: Lumalaki ng 1 ang pagitan (+1, +2, +3, +4), kaya +5 na: 11 + 5 = 16.
427974349.whyB: 15 repeats the last gap (+4) instead of increasing it.
427974349.text: What is the next number in the series: 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ...?

671024720.explanation: Each term is double the previous one plus 1: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31.
671024720.explanationTl: Bawat term ay doble ng nauna plus 1: 15 × 2 + 1 = 31.
671024720.whyB: 29 doubles 15 and subtracts 1 instead of adding 1.
671024720.whyD: 27 adds 12, treating the gaps as growing by 4.
671024720.steps:
1. The gaps are 2, 4, 8 — they double, so the next gap is 16.
2. 15 + 16 = 31.
(Same rule: each term × 2 + 1.)
671024720.hint: Look at the gaps between terms — how do they change?
671024720.stepsTl:
1. Ang pagitan ay 2, 4, 8 — dumodoble, kaya 16 ang susunod.
2. 15 + 16 = 31.
671024720.hintTl: Tingnan ang pagitan ng mga numero — paano ito nagbabago?

799606978.explanation: Each term goes up by 2, so 10 + 2 = 12.
799606978.text: What is the next number in the series: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, ...?

861080332.whyC: 252 adds 63 (an additive pattern) instead of multiplying.

1177479934.whyB: 120 adds 40 (the previous gap) instead of doubling.
1177479934.text: What is the next number in the series: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, ...?

1254511877.whyB: 96 adds 32 (the previous gap) instead of doubling.

1709679520.whyC: 72 adds 18 (an earlier term) instead of multiplying.

1787589291.explanation: The gaps are odd numbers (+3, +5, +7), so the next gap is +9: 17 + 9 = 26. (Each term is n² + 1.)
1787589291.explanationTl: Ang pagitan ay odd numbers (+3, +5, +7), kaya +9 na: 17 + 9 = 26.
1787589291.whyB: 25 is 5² but forgets the +1 (pattern is n² + 1).
1787589291.text: What is the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, ...?

2051560334.text: What is the next number in the series: 3, 12, 48, 192, ...?
2051560334.hint: The gaps grow fast — try dividing each term by the one before it.
2051560334.whyD: 240 adds 48 (an earlier term) instead of multiplying.
2051560334.hintTl: Mabilis lumaki — subukang i-divide ang bawat term sa nauna.

2139960336.whyD: 4 goes up although the series is decreasing.

1989361240.text: A training seminar runs for 3 weeks and 4 days with no breaks. How many days does it last?
1989361240.steps:
1. Convert weeks to days: 3 × 7 = 21.
2. Add the extra days: 21 + 4 = 25 days.
1989361240.hint: Change the weeks into days first, then add the extra days.
1989361240.whyA: 21 counts only the 3 weeks and drops the 4 extra days.
1989361240.whyB: 34 just writes 3 and 4 side by side.
1989361240.stepsTl:
1. Gawing days ang weeks: 3 × 7 = 21.
2. I-add ang sobrang days: 21 + 4 = 25.
1989361240.hintTl: Gawin munang days ang weeks, tapos i-add ang natitirang days.

185642614.text: If 3 apples cost ₱50, how much do 12 apples cost?
185642614.explanation: 12 apples is 4 times 3 apples, so the cost is 4 × ₱50 = ₱200.
185642614.steps:
1. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 groups of 3 apples.
2. Each group costs ₱50.
3. 4 × ₱50 = ₱200.
185642614.hint: How many groups of 3 apples are in 12 apples?
185642614.explanationTl: Ang 12 apples ay 4 na grupo ng 3, kaya 4 × ₱50 = ₱200.
185642614.stepsTl:
1. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 na grupo ng tig-3 apples.
2. ₱50 bawat grupo.
3. 4 × ₱50 = ₱200.
185642614.hintTl: Ilang grupo ng 3 apples ang nasa 12?

468619307.explanation: Each programmer codes 1 program in 10 days, so 5 programmers code 5 programs in the same 10 days.
468619307.whyB: 5 halves the time because the numbers were halved — but workers and work were both halved, so time stays the same.
468619307.whyC: 20 doubles the time for half the workers but forgets the work was also halved.
468619307.whyD: 15 is not supported by any step; the rate per programmer is unchanged.
468619307.explanationTl: Isang programmer = 1 program sa 10 days, kaya 5 programmers = 5 programs sa 10 days pa rin.

881178821.text: If 10 workers can complete a project in 10 days, how many days would 5 workers need at the same rate?
881178821.explanation: The project takes 10 × 10 = 100 worker-days, so 5 workers need 100 ÷ 5 = 20 days.
881178821.steps:
1. Total work = 10 workers × 10 days = 100 worker-days.
2. With 5 workers: 100 ÷ 5 = 20 days.
881178821.hint: Fewer workers means more days — find the total worker-days first.
881178821.whyB: 15 adds only 5 days for 5 fewer workers instead of using total worker-days.
881178821.whyC: 25 overshoots: 5 workers × 25 days = 125 worker-days, more than the 100 needed.
881178821.whyD: 10 assumes the time stays the same with half the workers.
881178821.explanationTl: Ang project ay 10 × 10 = 100 worker-days, kaya 5 workers ay 100 ÷ 5 = 20 days.
881178821.stepsTl:
1. Kabuuang trabaho = 10 × 10 = 100 worker-days.
2. Kung 5 workers: 100 ÷ 5 = 20 days.
881178821.hintTl: Mas kaunting tao, mas matagal — hanapin muna ang total worker-days.

892836642.text: If 3 workers can build a wall in 4 days, how many days would 6 workers need at the same rate?
892836642.explanation: The wall takes 3 × 4 = 12 worker-days, so 6 workers need 12 ÷ 6 = 2 days.
892836642.steps:
1. Total work = 3 workers × 4 days = 12 worker-days.
2. With 6 workers: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 days.
892836642.hint: More workers means fewer days — find the total worker-days first.
892836642.whyB: 3 subtracts 1 day instead of halving the time for double the workers.
892836642.whyD: 2.5 is not supported; doubling the workers exactly halves the 4 days.
892836642.explanationTl: Ang pader ay 3 × 4 = 12 worker-days, kaya 6 workers ay 12 ÷ 6 = 2 days.
892836642.stepsTl:
1. Kabuuang trabaho = 3 × 4 = 12 worker-days.
2. Kung 6 workers: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 days.
892836642.hintTl: Mas maraming tao, mas mabilis — hanapin muna ang total worker-days.

1358651343.explanation: Each mechanic repairs 1 car in 5 hours, so 10 mechanics repair 10 cars in the same 5 hours.
1358651343.whyB: 10 doubles the time because the numbers doubled — but workers and work both doubled.
1358651343.whyC: 2.5 halves the time for double the workers but forgets the work also doubled.
1358651343.whyD: 7.5 is not supported by any step; the rate per mechanic is unchanged.
1358651343.explanationTl: Isang mekaniko = 1 kotse sa 5 hours, kaya 10 mekaniko = 10 kotse sa 5 hours pa rin.

1380766250.text: Six farmers can harvest a rice field in 8 days. Working at the same rate, how many days would 4 farmers need?
1380766250.explanation: The job takes 6 × 8 = 48 farmer-days, so 4 farmers need 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
1380766250.steps:
1. Total work = 6 farmers × 8 days = 48 farmer-days.
2. With 4 farmers: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
1380766250.hint: Fewer workers means more days — find the total farmer-days first.
1380766250.whyA: 5⅓ treats it as direct proportion (8 × 4 ÷ 6); fewer farmers should take longer.
1380766250.whyB: 10 adds 2 days for 2 fewer farmers instead of using total farmer-days.
1380766250.whyD: 6 subtracts 2 days, as if fewer farmers worked faster.
1380766250.explanationTl: Ang trabaho ay 6 × 8 = 48 farmer-days, kaya 4 farmers ay 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
1380766250.stepsTl:
1. Kabuuang trabaho = 6 × 8 = 48 farmer-days.
2. Kung 4 farmers: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days.
1380766250.hintTl: Mas kaunting tao, mas matagal — hanapin muna ang total farmer-days.

1771433287.text: Nine builders finish 3 houses in 12 months. At the same rate, how many months would 6 builders need to finish 4 houses?
1771433287.explanation: One house takes 9 × 12 ÷ 3 = 36 builder-months, so 4 houses take 144 builder-months; 144 ÷ 6 = 24 months.
1771433287.steps:
1. Total work for 3 houses = 9 × 12 = 108 builder-months.
2. Per house: 108 ÷ 3 = 36 builder-months.
3. For 4 houses: 4 × 36 = 144 builder-months.
4. With 6 builders: 144 ÷ 6 = 24 months.
1771433287.hint: Find how many builder-months ONE house takes.
1771433287.whyA: 16 scales up for 4 houses (12 × 4 ÷ 3) but forgets there are fewer builders.
1771433287.whyC: 18 adjusts for fewer builders (12 × 9 ÷ 6) but forgets the extra house.
1771433287.whyD: 36 is the builder-months for one house, not the number of months.
1771433287.explanationTl: Isang bahay = 9 × 12 ÷ 3 = 36 builder-months, kaya 4 na bahay = 144; 144 ÷ 6 = 24 months.
1771433287.stepsTl:
1. Trabaho sa 3 bahay = 9 × 12 = 108 builder-months.
2. Bawat bahay: 108 ÷ 3 = 36.
3. Para sa 4 na bahay: 4 × 36 = 144.
4. Kung 6 builders: 144 ÷ 6 = 24 months.
1771433287.hintTl: Alamin muna kung ilang builder-months ang isang bahay.

1402275905.explanation: Day and night are a matched pair of opposites. The sun is the main light of the day sky and the moon is its counterpart in the night sky, so sun pairs with moon.
1402275905.hint: Think of what shines in the sky at the time that is the opposite of day.
1402275905.whyB: The sun itself is a star, so 'star' does not give the night-time counterpart of the sun.
1402275905.whyC: Light is what the sun gives off, not its opposite partner.
1402275905.whyD: The sky holds both sun and moon; it is not the counterpart of the sun.
1402275905.explanationTl: Magkapares ang day at night bilang magkasalungat. Ang sun ang ilaw ng araw, at ang moon naman ang katapat nito sa gabi, kaya sun : moon.
1402275905.hintTl: Isipin mo kung ano ang nasa langit sa oras na kabaligtaran ng day.

117669853.explanation: Opulent means very rich and luxurious. Its opposite is poor.
117669853.hint: Find the word that means the reverse of having great wealth and luxury.
117669853.whyA: Wealthy is a synonym of opulent, not an antonym.
117669853.whyC: Lavish means rich and abundant, which is close to opulent in meaning.
117669853.whyD: Affluent means wealthy, a synonym of opulent.
117669853.explanationTl: Ang opulent ay sobrang yaman at marangya. Kaya ang kabaligtaran nito ay poor.
117669853.hintTl: Hanapin mo ang salitang kabaligtaran ng pagiging mayaman at marangya.
